question: An investigation in relation to an offence under sections 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 70, 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 or under sections 4, 6, 8 or 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 shall be completed within...............from the date of recorded information.
explanation: Section 193(2) of the BNSS mandates that the investigation of rape cases and POCSO offences must be completed within two months from the date on which the information was recorded.

subject: BNSS
question: Which one of the following provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 provides that "The investigation in relation to an offence under sections 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 70, 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 or under sections 4, 6, 8 or 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 shall be completed within two months from the date on which the information was recorded by the officer in charge of the police station"?
explanation: Section 193(2) of the BNSS, 2023 sets out the specific two-month timeline for completing investigations in sexual offences.

subject: BNSS
question: "Police Report" means:-
options: Report lodged by the complainant in the police station
Report sent by officer in charge of police station to superior officer
A report forwarded by police officer to a magistrate under Sec. 193(3) of B.N.S.S.
Report entered in a case diary
explanation: The statutory definition of "Police Report" under Section 2(r) of the BNSS means a report forwarded by a police officer to a Magistrate under Section 193(3).

subject: BNSS
question: Report of police officer on completion of investigation under Section 193 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is called:-
explanation: The final report submitted under Section 193(3) is commonly referred to as a "Charge Sheet" if it recommends prosecution, or a "Closure Report" if no case is made out.

subject: BNSS
question: The S.H.O. of a Police Station is conducting investigation of a murder case. The custody period of 90 days of one accused is coming to an end but the investigation is not complete. The Investigating Officer may file partial charge-sheet while keeping investigation pending under:-
explanation: Section 193(9) of the BNSS permits the police to submit further reports (supplementary charge sheets) after conducting further investigation.

subject: BNSS
question: Section 193(9) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 deals with:-
explanation: Section 193(9) (corresponding to Section 173(8) of the old CrPC) recognizes the right of the police to conduct "further investigation" after a report has been forwarded to the Magistrate.

subject: BNSS
question: Further investigation within the meaning of section 193(9) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is:-
options: the continuation of the earlier investigation
fresh investigation ab initio wiping out the earlier investigation altogether
re-investigation ab initio wiping out the earlier investigation altogether
either the continuation of the earlier investigation or fresh investigation ab initio wiping out the earlier investigation altogether
explanation: "Further investigation" is a continuation of the initial investigation to gather additional evidence, distinct from a "fresh" or "de novo" investigation.

subject: BNSS
question: Additional challan in a case is:-
options: allowed with the permission of the Court
not allowed on the ground that no person can be tried for additional challan
allowed on the evidence found in additional investigation
explanation: Under Section 193(9), if the officer obtains further oral or documentary evidence, they can forward an additional report (challan) to the Magistrate.

subject: BNSS
question: In which judgment, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down that having taken cognizance of a case, the Magistrate cannot direct the Police to conduct further investigation:-
options: State of Haryana Vs. Choudhary Bhajan Lal, AIR 1992 SC 604
M/s. Jayanti Vitamin Vs. Chaitanya Kumar, AIR 1992 SC 1930
Amrutbhai Shambhubhai Patel Vs. Sumanbhai Kantibhai Patel & Ors., AIR 2017 SC 774
Hemant Dhasmana Vs. CBI, AIR 2001 SC 2721
explanation: In Amrutbhai Shambhubhai Patel v. Sumanbhai Kantibhai Patel (2017), the Supreme Court ruled that once cognizance has been taken and the accused has appeared, a Magistrate cannot order further investigation suo motu.

subject: BNSS
question: Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 applies when the officer-in-charge of a police station receives information that a person has committed suicide?
explanation: Section 194 of the BNSS (corresponding to Section 174 of the old CrPC) governs the procedure for police inquiries and reports on suicides and unnatural deaths (inquest proceedings).

subject: BNSS
question: What is primary object of inquest report under Section 194 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
options: To know the name of the assailants of the deceased
To know the motive of the commission of offence
To know the apparent cause of death
To know the place of occurrence
explanation: The scope of an inquiry under Section 194 is limited to finding the apparent cause of death, describing the wounds, fractures, or marks found on the body, and noting the weapon used.

subject: BNSS
question: When the officer-in-charge of the police station receives information that a person has committed suicide, he will immediately report to the:-
explanation: Section 194(1) requires the officer to give intimation to the nearest Executive Magistrate empowered to hold inquests.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 a Magistrate has the power to enquire into the cause of death?
explanation: Section 196 of the BNSS (corresponding to Section 176 of the old CrPC) provides for a magisterial inquiry into the cause of death of a person in police or judicial custody.

subject: BNSS
question: An inquest report must contain:-
explanation: The primary purpose of the inquest under Section 196 is to record the apparent cause of death of the deceased.

subject: BNSS
question: Where the person dies or disappear or woman is raped while such person or woman is in custody of police authorized by a Magistrate, an inquiry in addition to inquiry or investigation held by the police, shall be held by:-
options: Judicial Magistrate within whose local jurisdiction the offence has been committed
explanation: Section 196(1A) of the BNSS mandates that in cases of custodial death, disappearance, or rape, an inquiry must be conducted by the Judicial Magistrate or Metropolitan Magistrate, in addition to the police inquiry.

subject: BNSS
question: An inquiry into the cause of death must be held, in a case where the death has occurred before the person after arrest could be produced before a Magistrate, by:-
options: Judicial Magistrate in addition to inquiry by the police
explanation: Section 196(1A) makes a Judicial Magistrate's inquiry mandatory in cases of death occurring while the person is in police custody.

subject: BNSS
question: Ordinarily place of trial is:-
options: Where the offence has been committed
explanation: Section 197 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 177 CrPC) establishes the general rule of territorial jurisdiction: every offence shall ordinarily be inquired into and tried by a Court within whose local jurisdiction it was committed.

subject: BNSS
question: With regard to the place of inquiry or trial, which of the following statements is false :-
options: When it is uncertain in which of several local areas an offence was committed, it may be inquired into or tried by a Court having jurisdiction over any of such local areas
Where an offence is committed partly in one local area and partly in another, it may be inquired into or tried by a Court having jurisdiction over any of such local areas
Where an offence is a continuing one, and continues to be committed in more local areas than one, it may be inquired into or tried by a court having jurisdiction over any of such local areas
When it consists of several acts done in different local areas, it may be inquired into or tried by a court having jurisdiction over the local area in which first of such acts was committed.
explanation: Under Section 200 of the BNSS (old Section 178 CrPC), where an offence consists of several acts done in different local areas, it may be tried by a Court having jurisdiction over any of such local areas, not just the first one.

subject: BNSS
question: A minor girl lived with her father at Indore. She became intimate with the accused and ran away with the accused from Indore to Bhopal in a taxi. After some time they eventually settled in Mumbai. An offence of kidnapping may be tried :-
explanation: Under Section 201(2) of the BNSS (old Section 181(2) CrPC), the offence of kidnapping or abduction may be inquired into or tried by a Court within whose local jurisdiction the person was kidnapped, conveyed, or concealed.

subject: BNSS
question: A was wounded in Uttar Pradesh and dies of his wounds in Bhopal. The offence of causing A's death may be inquired into and tried in :-
explanation: Section 199 of the BNSS (old Section 179 CrPC) provides that where an act is an offence by reason of its consequence, it may be tried by a Court where the act was done or where the consequence ensued.

subject: BNSS
question: An offence of theft can be tried by a Court under whose jurisdiction :-
options: the stolen property is found in possession of thief
the stolen property is kept by the accused knowing it to be stolen
explanation: Section 201(3) of the BNSS (old Section 181(3) CrPC) allows the offence of theft or receiving stolen property to be tried where the theft occurred or where the stolen property was possessed/received.

subject: BNSS
question: 'X' sends an e-mail to 'Y' from Delhi threatening 'Y' that certain photographs showing 'Y' in a compromising position with a woman shall be posted on the net, if 'Y' does not pay Rs. 1,000,000/- to 'X'. 'Y' accesses the e-mail at his office in Kolkata. The offence can be inquired into or tried by a court at:-
options: Anywhere in India because the e-mail can be accessed anywhere in India
explanation: Under Section 202 of the BNSS (old Section 182 CrPC), offences committed by letters or telecommunication messages can be tried either where the messages were sent (Delhi) or where they were received/accessed (Kolkata).

subject: BNSS
question: Section 203 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Offence committed on journey or voyage):-
options: applies to voyage on the high seas.
does not apply to voyage on high seas.
applies to voyage within India as well as on voyage on high seas.
explanation: Section 203 of the BNSS (corresponding to Section 183 CrPC) governs offences committed on a journey or voyage. It is restricted to territorial limits and does not apply to voyages on the high seas outside India's territory.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following is correctly matched?
options: Ordinary place of inquiry and trial — Section 199
Offences triable where act is done — Section 198
Offences committed on voyage and journey — Section 203
Offences committed by letters, etc. — Section 208
explanation: Offences committed on a journey or voyage are governed by Section 203 of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 183 CrPC). The other options contain incorrect section matches.

subject: BNSS
question: When there is a dispute between two courts relating to the exercise of jurisdiction in a criminal matter and said courts are under the subordination of different High Courts, the matter shall be decided under section 206 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 by the:-
options: High Court of the larger State
High Court within whose area the proceedings first commenced
explanation: Section 206 of the BNSS (old Section 186 CrPC) provides that if the courts are subordinate to different High Courts, the dispute is decided by the High Court within the local limits of whose appellate criminal jurisdiction the proceedings were first commenced.

subject: BNSS
question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 where two or more courts have taken cognizance of the same offence and a question arises as to which of them ought to try that offence, the question shall be decided:-
options: if the court are subordinate to the same High Court by that High Court
if the Courts are not subordinate to the same High Court, by the High Court within the local limits of whose appellate criminal jurisdiction the proceeding were first commenced.
explanation: Under Section 206 of the BNSS, if the courts are subordinate to the same High Court, that High Court decides. If they are subordinate to different High Courts, the High Court where the proceedings first commenced decides. (Thus, statement ii and iii are the correct parameters).

subject: BNSS
question: 'A' and four accomplices absconded after kidnapping 'G' from New Delhi, confining her at Gurugram in Haryana for ransom, and then taking her to Uttar Pradesh. Investigation reports are filed seeking trial in Gurugram and New Delhi, and cognizance is taken in both. If a jurisdictional dispute arises, which court decides the forum?
options: The High Court of Judicature at Allahabad shall decide as to Court at which place will inquire or try the offences
The High Court of Punjab and Haryana shall decide as to Court at which place will inquire into or try the offences
The High Court of Delhi shall decide as to Court at which place will inquire into or try the offences
Only the Court at New Delhi can inquire into or try the offences since that is the place from where the kidnapping took place.
explanation: Under Section 206 of the BNSS, where courts subordinate to different High Courts have taken cognizance, the High Court within whose jurisdiction the proceedings first commenced has the power to decide. (The book answer key lists option A).

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 provides for dealing with offences committed outside India?
explanation: Section 208 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 188 of the old CrPC) deals with offences committed outside India by a citizen of India or by any person on an aircraft or vessel registered in India.

subject: BNSS
question: An offence is committed by a British citizen on an aircraft registered in India. The offender may be dealt with under which provision of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 208(b) extends India's criminal jurisdiction to any person (regardless of citizenship) committing an offence on any ship or aircraft registered in India.

subject: BNSS
question: Where two courts subordinate to the same High Court have taken cognizance and a question arises as to which of them shall try that offence:-
options: the question shall be decided by any one of these Courts
the question cannot be decided by any court
the question shall be decided by the concerned High Court
the question can be left to the parties
explanation: Under Section 206(a) of the BNSS, if the courts are subordinate to the same High Court, that High Court holds the statutory authority to resolve the jurisdictional dispute.

subject: BNSS
question: 'A' who is a citizen of India commits murder in Uganda. He is arrested in Delhi. He can be tried and convicted of murder:-
options: only in that country of which the deceased was a citizen
in any one of the above
explanation: Under Section 208, a citizen of India who commits an offence outside India can be tried in India at any place where he may be found (which in this case is Delhi).

subject: BNSS
question: An offence is committed outside India by a citizen of India. Such offence shall be inquired or tried in India with the previous sanction of:-
explanation: The proviso to Section 208 of the BNSS stipulates that no such offence shall be inquired into or tried in India except with the previous sanction of the Central Government.

subject: BNSS
question: A Magistrate may take cognizance of an offence:-
explanation: Section 210(1) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 190(1) CrPC) provides three modes of taking cognizance: upon receiving a complaint, upon a police report, or upon information/knowledge suo motu.

subject: BNSS
question: Which court may take cognizance of offences under section 210 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
options: Any Magistrate of the first class
Any Magistrate of the second class specially empowered in this behalf
explanation: Under Section 210, any Magistrate of the first class, and any Magistrate of the second class specially empowered by the Chief Judicial Magistrate under Section 210(2), may take cognizance.

subject: BNSS
question: A magistrate cannot take cognizance of an offence:-
options: On the basis of direction given by District Judge
On the basis of Police report
On the basis of his own knowledge
explanation: A District Judge (Civil Court) has no authority under Section 210 to direct a Judicial Magistrate to take cognizance of a criminal offence.

subject: BNSS
question: Who can take cognizance under section 210 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 210 specifically empowers Judicial Magistrates (Magistrate of the first class or specially empowered second class) to take cognizance of offences.

subject: BNSS
question: Under section 210(2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 who may empower any Magistrate of second class to take cognizance of offences?
explanation: Section 210(2) of the BNSS provides that the Chief Judicial Magistrate may empower any Magistrate of the second class to take cognizance of such offences as are within his competence to inquire into or try.

subject: BNSS
question: A Magistrate may take cognizance of an offence on complaint if in his opinion:-
options: There is sufficient ground for conviction
There is prima facie no probable defence of accused
There is sufficient ground for proceeding
explanation: For taking cognizance and issuing process, the Magistrate only needs to be satisfied that there is "sufficient ground for proceeding" (prima facie case), not sufficient ground for conviction.

subject: BNSS
question: A Magistrate may take cognizance under Section 210 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 of any offence:-
options: upon receiving a complaint of facts which constitute such offence or upon his own knowledge that such offence has been committed
upon a police report of such facts
upon information received from any person other than a police officer, that such offence has been committed
explanation: All three clauses (a, b, and c) of Section 210(1) are valid grounds upon which a Magistrate can take cognizance.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the powers of a Magistrate regarding a police report?
options: ignore the conclusion reached at by the Investigating Officer (IO) and apply his mind independently
not ignore the conclusions reached at by the IO and apply his mind independently
ignore the conclusions reached at by the IO and apply his mind independently only upon statements of witnesses recorded by the police in case diary and material collected during investigation
not ignore the conclusions reached by the IO under any circumstances
explanation: A Magistrate is a judicial officer and is not bound by the final opinion/conclusion of the investigating officer; he must apply his mind independently to the facts disclosed in the report.

subject: BNSS
question: In which case, it was held that at the time of framing charge or taking cognizance, the accused has no right to produce any material?
options: Anil Rai v. State of Bihar
State of Orissa v. Debendra Nath Padhi
Bani Singh v. State of U.P.
Pratap Singh v. State of Jharkhand
explanation: In State of Orissa v. Debendra Nath Padhi (2005), a three-judge bench of the Supreme Court held that the accused has no right to produce any defense material at the stage of framing of charge or taking cognizance.

subject: BNSS
question: Which Section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 prohibits a Court of Session to take cognizance of any offence as a Court of Original Jurisdiction unless the case has been committed to it by a Magistrate under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 213 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 193 of the old CrPC) bars the Court of Session from taking cognizance of any offence as a court of original jurisdiction unless committed to it.

subject: BNSS
question: Cognizance of offence as a Court of original jurisdiction is taken by Sessions Court:-
options: Under Section 193 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Under Section 210 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Under Section 213 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Under Section 175 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Under Section 213 of the BNSS, the Court of Session takes cognizance of cases committed to it by a competent Magistrate.

subject: BNSS
question: Which one of the following is true about the Sessions Court:-
options: Can take cognizance only on committal
Can take cognizance on the recommendation of District Magistrate
Can take cognizance provided the charge sheet is submitted by Superintendent of Police
explanation: Except where specifically provided by law (such as defamation of high dignitaries under Section 222(2)), the Court of Session can take cognizance only after a case is committed to it.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, a magistrate can commit a case to Court of Session which is not exclusively triable by the Court of Session if it appears to him that the case is such that:-
options: Which could not be adequately punished by him
Some question of law of unusual difficulty is likely to arise
He has no jurisdiction to try the case
The case is one which ought to be tried by the court of session
explanation: Under Section 363 of the BNSS (old Section 323 CrPC), if at any stage before signing judgment it appears to the Magistrate that the case is one which ought to be tried by the Court of Session, he shall commit it.

subject: BNSS
question: The provisions of Section 215 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 require:-
explanation: Section 215 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 195 of the old CrPC) mandates that no court shall take cognizance of specified public administration/justice offences except on the complaint in writing of the concerned public servant or court.

subject: BNSS
question: As per Section 215 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, cognizance of offences punishable under Section 206 to 223 (both inclusive but excluding section 209) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 can be taken on:-
explanation: Cognizance of offences against public authority under Section 215 must strictly be taken only on a written complaint by the public servant or their authorized superior.

subject: BNSS
question: If the forgery was committed while the document was in the custody of a Court, then prosecution can be launched only with a complaint made by the:-
explanation: Under Section 215(1)(b)(ii), if forgery is committed in respect of a document produced or given in evidence in a proceeding in any Court, the complaint must be in writing by that Court.

subject: BNSS
question: If the forgery was committed while the document was in the custody of a Court, then cognizance of the offence of forgery can be taken only on the basis of written complaint made by the:-
options: Court or officer authorized in this behalf
explanation: The written complaint must be submitted by the Court itself, or by an officer of the Court authorized by it in writing.

subject: BNSS
question: In a case of threatening to a witness or any other person to give false evidence, complaint may be filed by:-
explanation: Section 216 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 195A of the old CrPC) provides that a complaint for threatening a witness (Section 351 BNS) may be filed by the witness or any other person aggrieved by such threat.

subject: BNSS
question: The prosecution of Judges and public servants are provided in:-
explanation: Section 218 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 197 of the old CrPC) contains the provisions requiring prior sanction for prosecuting judges and public servants.

subject: BNSS
question: For which of the following offences alleged to have been committed by a public servant while acting in the discharge of official duty is previous sanction under Section 218 of the BNSS, 2023 required?
options: Any offence alleged to have been committed under Section 199, Section 200
Any offence alleged to have been committed under Section 74, Section 75, Section 76, Section 77 or Section 78.
Any offence alleged to have been committed under Section 101
Any offence alleged to have been committed under Section 79
explanation: Section 101 of the BNS (kidnapping/abduction). The other options refer to sexual offences (such as Section 74-78 BNS) where the protection of sanction is explicitly excluded by the code.

subject: BNSS
question: Public servant 'A' while discharging his official functions, issues a document with incorrect particulars knowing that by this action, he is likely to harm another public servant 'B'. The public servant 'A' is responsible for which of the following offence?
explanation: A public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury is punished under Section 199 of the BNS, 2023, which is distinct from forgery, cheating, or creating a false document.

subject: BNSS
question: No member of the Armed Forces of the Union shall be arrested for anything done in the discharge of his official duties except after attaining the consent of:-
explanation: Section 42 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 45 of the old CrPC) protects members of the Armed Forces from arrest for official acts except with the consent of the Central Government.

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following case it has been held that Section 197 of Criminal Procedure Code [Now, Section 218 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023] is constitutionally valid?
options: Joseph Shine Vs. Union of India
Navtej Johar Vs. Union of India
Naaz Foundation Vs. Union of India
Subrahamanyam Swami Vs. Union of India
explanation: In Subramanian Swamy v. Manmohan Singh (2012), the Supreme Court discussed and upheld the constitutional validity and scope of the prior sanction requirement.

subject: BNSS
question: Which section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 provides for prosecution for offences against marriage?
explanation: Section 219 of the BNSS (corresponding to Section 198 of the old CrPC) contains the provisions restricting cognizance of offences against marriage except on a complaint by an aggrieved party.

subject: BNSS
question: Cognizance of an offence punishable under Sections 81 to 84 (both inclusive) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 shall be taken, ordinarily, upon a complaint by which of the following persons?
options: A person interested in social work
explanation: Offences against marriage (Sections 81 to 84 BNS, e.g., bigamy) require a complaint by the person aggrieved by the offence under Section 219(1).

subject: BNSS
question: Under section 219 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, no court can take cognizance of an offence against marriage [punishable under Sections 81 to 84 (both inclusive) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023] unless a complaint is made by:-
options: Some person who is aggrieved by the offence.
explanation: The court is barred from taking cognizance unless the complaint is filed by the aggrieved person (e.g., the first spouse).

subject: BNSS
question: Cognizance of offence under Section 85 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Cruelty by husband or relatives) can be taken on:-
options: On the complaint of the person aggrieved
On the complaint of the father, mother, brother or sister of the person aggrieved
explanation: Under Section 220 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 198A CrPC), cognizance of cruelty can be taken upon a police report, or a complaint by the wife, or her parents/siblings (or other relatives with Court permission).

subject: BNSS
question: Cognizance of the offence of defamation under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 can be taken:-
options: on a complaint made by an aggrieved party
explanation: Under Section 222(1) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 199 CrPC), no Court shall take cognizance of defamation except upon a complaint made by some person aggrieved by the offence.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which of the following section of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, a court of session has the original jurisdiction to take cognizance of defamation without committal of case:-
explanation: Section 222(2) of the BNSS provides a special exception where the Court of Session can take direct cognizance of defamation against high public dignitaries upon a written complaint by the Public Prosecutor.

subject: BNSS
question: For a Sessions Court to take cognizance of defamation committed against the governor of a state, the complaint must be made within.............from the date on which the offence is alleged to have been committed.
explanation: Under Section 222(5) of the BNSS, 2023, the complaint by the Public Prosecutor must be made within six months from the date of the alleged offence.

subject: BNSS
question: The judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of K.K. Mishra Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2018 SC 374 explains:-
options: The rationale for special procedure provided in Section 199 of Cr.P.C. (Now, Section 222 of B.N.S.S.)
The powers of Court of Sessions in matter of bail
The distinction between interim bail and regular bail
explanation: In K.K. Mishra v. State of M.P. (2018), the Supreme Court analyzed the special procedure for prosecuting defamation of public servants and the criteria for invoking it.

subject: BNSS
question: Under section 223 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 recording of pre-summoning evidence may be dispensed with if:-
options: The complaint is supported by an affidavit of the complainant
The complaint is made in writing by a public servant
The Magistrate feels that ends of justice require pre-summoning evidence to be dispensed with.
explanation: Under Section 223(1) proviso (a), if the complaint is made in writing by a public servant acting in the discharge of official duties or a Court, the Magistrate need not examine them.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the magistrate need not examine the complainant and the witnesses:-
options: if the complaint is supported by the affidavit of the complainant
if the complaint is made in writing by a public servant in the discharge of his official duties
if the complainant is senior citizen
explanation: The examination of the complainant on oath is dispensed with when a written complaint is submitted by a public servant or a court.

subject: BNSS
question: In a private complaint case process can be issued against an accused after:-
options: Complaint in writing is presented to the Court
Complainant's statement on oath is recorded
The Magistrate is of the opinion that there is sufficient ground to proceed with the case.
Police upon investigation submit a report that there is sufficient ground to proceed with the case.
explanation: Under Section 227(1) (old Section 204), a Magistrate issues process (summons/warrant) only when he is of the opinion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding.

subject: BNSS
question: Upon perusal of a complaint alleging offence of cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property during the course of business transaction between two firms, the jurisdictional Magistrate may:-
options: Take cognizance and examine upon oath the complainant and the witnesses who are present.
Examine upon oath the complainant and the witnesses who are present and then consider if cognizance be taken or not.
Decline to take cognizance if the offence alleged is triable exclusively by the court of Sessions.
Issue summons to the accused if prima facie satisfied on basis of affidavit of the complainant and then examine the complainant and his witnesses in the presence of the accused.
explanation: The Magistrate must first take cognizance and then record the statements of the complainant and witnesses on oath under Section 223.

subject: BNSS
question: If a complaint in writing is made to a Magistrate who is not competent to take cognizance of the offence:-
options: he shall return it for presentation to the proper court with an endorsement to that effect.
explanation: Under Section 224(a) of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 201 CrPC), if the complaint is in writing and the Magistrate is incompetent, he must return it with an endorsement for presentation to the proper Court.

subject: BNSS
question: If it appears to the Magistrate that the offence complained of is triable exclusively by the Court of Session, he under section 225 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 postponing the issue of process against the accused:-
options: Shall commit the case to the court of Session
May direct an investigation to be made by a police officer
Shall call upon the complainant to produce all his witness and examine them on oath
Shall return the complaint for presentation to produce before the Court of Session.
explanation: Section 225 proviso of the BNSS (old Section 202 proviso) mandates that in Sessions-triable cases, the Magistrate shall call upon the complainant to produce all witnesses and examine them on oath before process is issued.

subject: BNSS
question: Direction to the police to investigate u/s. 225 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023:-
options: Cannot be given without examining the complainant on oath.
Can be given without examining the complainant on oath.
Can be given before or after examining the complainant on oath.
Cannot be given in any circumstances.
explanation: Under Section 225(1) proviso (b), a Magistrate cannot direct a police investigation in a complaint case unless the complainant and witnesses present have been examined on oath.

subject: BNSS
question: The distinction between a police investigation ordered under Section 156(3) and one directed under Section 202 of Cr.P.C. [Now, between Section 175(3) and Section 225 of BNSS, 2023] has been clearly brought out by the Supreme Court in:-
options: Devarapalli Lakshminarayana Reddy v. V. Narayana Reddy
Smt. Nagawwa v. Veerama Shivalingappa Konjalgi
Dr. S.S. Khanna v. Chief Secretary
explanation: In Devarapalli Lakshminarayana Reddy v. V. Narayana Reddy (1976), the Supreme Court held that Section 156(3) operates at the pre-cognizance stage (police investigation), while Section 202 operates at the post-cognizance stage to help the Magistrate decide whether to issue process.

subject: BNSS
question: After dismissal of a complaint under Section 226, a fresh similar complaint on the same facts:-
options: Is not banned but will be entertained only in exceptional circumstances
Is not banned and will be entertained in all circumstances
explanation: Under the rule in Pramatha Nath Talukdar v. Saroj Ranjan Sarkar, a second complaint on the same facts is maintainable only under exceptional circumstances (e.g., manifest error, miscarriage of justice, or new evidence).

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 226 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, a magistrate may dismiss a complaint for which of the following reasons?
options: Magistrate is of opinion that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding
Magistrate is of opinion that there is not adequate evidence to convict the accused
Magistrate conclusively finds that accused is no more alive
In all of the above circumstances.
explanation: Section 226 (old Section 203) provides that the Magistrate may dismiss the complaint if, after considering the statements and result of inquiry/investigation, he is of the opinion that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding.

subject: BNSS
question: A magistrate dismisses a complaint after inquiry holding that identity of the accused is not disclosed in complaint. The order of the magistrate is:-
options: correct since it is mandatory to describe the identity of accused
correct even if the identity is disclosed in the inquiry it is not revealed from the complaint
incorrect since it is not mandatory to describe the identity of accused in complaint
incorrect since the proper course for the magistrate was to reject the complaint
explanation: It is not mandatory to state the name or identity of the accused in the complaint if it is unknown; the identity can be established during the inquiry or investigation.

subject: BNSS
question: Filing of list of witnesses by the complainant before issuance of summons or warrant to the accused under Section 227 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is:-
explanation: Section 227(2) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 204(2) CrPC) states that no summons or warrant shall be issued against the accused until a list of the prosecution witnesses has been filed.

subject: BNSS
question: Order for dismissal of complaint under sub-section (4) of section 227 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023:-
options: Can be directed to file new complaint
explanation: A dismissal of a complaint is a final order affecting the rights of the complainant, and it can be challenged by filing a revision petition.

subject: BNSS
question: A Magistrate may dispense with personal attendance of accused under:-
explanation: Section 228 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 205 of the old CrPC) provides that a Magistrate may dispense with the personal attendance of the accused and permit him to appear by his pleader.

subject: BNSS
question: Whether a person can send fine amount through postal department, without appearing in the court in some petty offences, if yes under what provision:-
explanation: Section 229 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 206 of the old CrPC) allows the accused in petty cases to transmit his plea of guilty and the fine by post or messenger.

subject: BNSS
question: Special summon under section 229 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 can be issued by:-
options: By magistrate as well as the court of sessions
explanation: Section 229(1) explicitly vest the power to issue special summons for petty offences in the Magistrate taking cognizance.

subject: BNSS
question: In petty offences the accused may plead guilty:-
options: above and also by transmitting plea through post or messenger
explanation: Under Section 229(1), the accused may plead guilty in person, through his pleader, or by transmitting the plea and the fine amount through post or messenger.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 229 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, 'petty offence' means:-
options: any offence punishable with fine only
any offence punishable under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939
any offence punishable only with fine not exceeding Five thousand rupees
explanation: Under Section 229(2) BNSS, a "petty offence" means any offence punishable only with fine not exceeding five thousand rupees, but does not include any offence so punishable under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

subject: BNSS
question: The maximum amount of fine specified in cases of petty offence under Section 229 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is:-
explanation: The ceiling for petty offence fine under Section 229 is set at five thousand rupees.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which of the following Sections of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 the accused shall be supplied the copy of Police report and other documents by the Magistrate?
explanation: Section 230 of the BNSS (corresponding to Section 207 of the old CrPC) mandates the supply of the police report, FIR, and other statements to the accused free of cost.

subject: BNSS
question: Committal proceedings under section 232 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 are in the nature of:-
explanation: Committal proceedings under Section 232 (old Section 209 CrPC) are considered an "inquiry" because they are conducted by a Magistrate prior to trial to determine if the case must be tried by the Court of Session.

subject: BNSS
question: A criminal case can be committed to the Court of Sessions by Judicial Magistrate under:-
explanation: A case can be committed either under Section 232 (when exclusively triable by Sessions) or Section 363 (when the Magistrate feels the case ought to be tried by Sessions).

subject: BNSS
question: A case can be committed to the Court of Session by a Magistrate under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 under:-
explanation: Section 232 governs mandatory committal, and Section 363 (old Section 323 CrPC) governs committal at a later stage of inquiry/trial.

subject: BNSS
question: Under section 232 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 which of the following cases can be committed to the court of sessions by a magistrate, if it appears to the magistrate that offence is triable exclusively by the court of sessions:-
options: A case instituted on police report
A case instituted otherwise than on a police report
Both a case instituted on police report and a case instituted otherwise than on a police report as well
explanation: Under Section 232, the Magistrate must commit the case to the Court of Session whether it is a police report case (clause a) or a private complaint case (clause b).

subject: BNSS
question: A charge-sheet is filed under section 103 of the BNS, 2023 against five accused: A, B, C, D, and E. A and B are absconding, C is exempted from personal appearance, D and E are present. The case can be committed to Sessions Court against:-
explanation: Committal is of the "case" itself, not individual accused persons. Therefore, the entire case is committed to the Court of Session against all five accused.

subject: BNSS
question: When can the provision of Section 233 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 be invoked?
options: When there is a complaint case and police is also investigating the matter
When there is a complaint case but police is not investigating the matter
When there is a complaint case and police has already completed investigation and submitted a final report
explanation: Section 233 of the BNSS (corresponding to Section 210 of the old CrPC) is designed to stay complaint case proceedings when a police investigation is ongoing for the same offence.

subject: BNSS
question: In case of merger of the complaint with the Police report, the procedure to be followed for the trial shall be:-
options: The procedure of the complaint case
The procedure of the case instituted on the police report
The procedure of both as per convenience during the trial
The procedure as directed by the Magistrate
explanation: Section 233(2) mandates that if the police submit a report and the court takes cognizance, both cases shall be tried together as if both were instituted on a police report.

subject: BNSS
question:
If, in a complaint case it is made to appear to Magistrate that an investigation by the police is in progress in relation to the same offence, which of the following order(s) a Magistrate may pass under Section 233 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
I. Return the complaint to be re-filed after police investigation.
II. Stay the proceeding of inquiry or trial on such complaint.
III. Call a report from the Investigating Officer.
IV. Refer the complaint for investigation by police.
V. Refer the complaint to Chief Judicial Magistrate.
explanation: Under Section 233(1), the Magistrate shall stay the complaint proceedings and call for a report on the matter from the police officer conducting the investigation.

subject: BNSS
question: If the police report does not relate to any accused in the complaint case or if the Magistrate does not take cognizance of any offence on the police report:-
options: he shall proceed with the inquiry or trial, which was stayed by him
he shall not proceed with the inquiry or trial, which was stayed by him
explanation: Under Section 233(3), if the police report does not lead to cognizance or relates to different accused, the Magistrate must resume the stayed complaint case.

subject: BNSS
question: The provision relating to the charge is given under:-
explanation: Chapter XVIII of the BNSS, 2023 (containing Sections 234 to 247) deals with 'The Charge'.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following is not a mandatory content of a charge?
options: Description of family background of the accused
Specific name of the offence as per the law which provides the offence
In case of unspecific name of the offence, definition of the offence
Particulars of time and place of the alleged offence
explanation: Under Section 234 and 235, the charge must contain the offence, law, time, place, and person against whom the offence was committed. Family background is irrelevant.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, a charge shall be written in the:-
explanation: Section 234(2) of the BNSS (old Section 211(2) CrPC) states: "The charge shall be written in the language of the Court."

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following statement is true?
options: 'A' is accused of cheating 'B' at a given time and place. The charge must set out the manner in which 'A' cheated 'B'.
'A' is accused of the theft of a certain article at a certain time and place. The charge need set out the manner in which the theft was effected.
'A' is accused of murder of 'B' at a given time and place. The charge need state the manner in which 'A' murdered 'B'.
explanation: Under Section 236 (old Section 213 CrPC), when the nature of the case is such that the particulars mentioned in Section 234 and 235 do not give the accused sufficient notice, the charge must contain the manner of commission (e.g. cheating).

subject: BNSS
question: 'A' is accused of cheating 'B' at a given time and place:-
options: The charge need not set out the manner in which 'A' cheated 'B'.
The charge must set out the manner in which 'A' cheated 'B'.
Whether the manner is set out or not is to be decided by the court.
explanation: Cheating requires the specific manner to be stated in the charge to satisfy the requirements of Section 236 BNSS.

subject: BNSS
question: An error or omission in the framing of a charge:-
options: is material in all circumstances shall vitiate the trial
is material only if has occasioned failure of Justice
is material and the accused is liable to be acquitted
explanation: Under Section 238 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 215 CrPC), no error or omission in stating the offence or particulars shall be regarded as material unless the accused was misled and it has occasioned a failure of justice.

subject: BNSS
question: The effect of error in stating the required particulars in the charge, shall be regarded material under which of the following circumstances?
options: When the accused is misled by the error.
When a material witness becomes hostile.
When the accused is declared absconded.
explanation: An error is material only if the accused is misled by the error and it has caused a failure of justice.

subject: BNSS
question: A is charged with cheating B, and the manner in which he cheated B is not set out in the charge. There were many transactions between A and B, and A had no means of knowing to which of them the charge referred, and offered no defence. The Court may infer from such facts that the omission to set out the manner of the cheating was, in the case, an error:-
options: not material as 'A' has not been misled
explanation: This is Illustration (b) to Section 238 BNSS. Since the accused had no means of identifying the transaction and offered no defence, he was misled, making the error material.

subject: BNSS
question: "A" is charged with murder of Ajay on 21.08.2024. In fact, the name of victim was Ajoy and offence was committed on 20.08.2024. The evidence adduced by prosecution correctly mentioned the name of the victim and the date of offence and he cross-examined the witnesses accordingly. The trial ends in conviction:-
options: The trial is vitiated because of the error in charge.
The trial is vitiated because it is a material irregularity.
The error is inconsequential as accused was not thereby misled.
explanation: This is Illustration (a) to Section 238 BNSS. Since the accused was not misled (as shown by his cross-examination), the spelling error and date discrepancy are immaterial.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which section of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 addition or alteration of charge has been provided?
explanation: Section 239 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 216 of the old CrPC) provides for the addition or alteration of any charge by the Court.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which provision of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, Court has the power to alter charge?
explanation: The power to alter a charge is found under Section 239 of the BNSS.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 239 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the Court has the power to:-
options: Only add to the charge(s) already framed
Only alter the charge(s) already framed
neither to alter nor to add to the charge(s) already framed
add to and alter the charge(s) both
explanation: Under Section 239(1), the Court has concurrent power to both alter existing charges and add new charges at any stage before judgment.

subject: BNSS
question: A Court may alter or add to a charge:-
options: Only before evidence of prosecution is closed
Only Appellate Court may alter charge
At any time before judgment is pronounced
explanation: Section 239(1) explicitly permits the Court to alter or add to any charge at any time before the judgment is pronounced.

subject: BNSS
question: The Court may alter the charges framed against the accused:-
options: Before examination of accused u/s 351 of B.N.S.S.
At any time before judgment is pronounced.
explanation: The statutory power to alter the charge is open-ended until the final pronouncement of the judgment.

subject: BNSS
question: Any court may alter or add to any charge:-
options: before examination of an accused under Section 351 of B.N.S.S.
after examination of an accused under Section 351 of B.N.S.S. but before examination of defence witnesses.
before examination of any prosecution witness.
at any time before the judgment is pronounced.
explanation: Section 239(1) lays down that the alteration/addition can happen at any time before judgment.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 239 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, any Court may alter or add to any charge at any time:-
explanation: The ultimate deadline for altering or adding to a charge is the pronouncement of the judgment.

subject: BNSS
question: Any defect in the charge:-
options: Can be cured by amending it in any case
Cannot be cured if such amendments is likely to cause serious prejudice to the accused
Can be cured by amending it though it causes prejudice to the accused
Can be cured by amending it with a direction to retrial if such amendment is causing prejudice to the accused
explanation: If the charge alteration is likely to prejudice the accused or prosecutor, the Court can either direct a new trial or adjourn the trial under Section 239(4).

subject: BNSS
question: 'A' is tried for causing grievous hurt to 'V' and convicted. After the completion of the trial, 'V' dies as a consequence of the injuries suffered. The State now wants to prosecute 'A' on a charge of culpable homicide:-
options: It is not permissible because the State ought to have anticipated the consequence of the acts committed while prosecuting 'A' on the lesser charge.
It is not permissible because it would amount to double jeopardy.
It is permissible because the consequence of the acts committed had not happened at the time 'A' was convicted.
It is permissible because the prerogative is of the State.
explanation: Under Section 337(3) of the BNSS (old Section 300(3) CrPC), a person can be tried for a separate offence (culpable homicide) if the consequence (death) had not occurred at the time of the first conviction.

subject: BNSS
question: Whenever a charge is altered or added to by the court after the trial has commenced:-
options: The prosecution has a right to recall or re-summon any witness who has already been examined.
The accused has no right to recall or re-summon any witness who has already been examined.
The prosecution has no right to call any further witnesses.
explanation: Section 240 of the BNSS (old Section 217 CrPC) grants both the prosecutor and the accused the right to recall or re-summon any witness who has already been examined when a charge is altered.

subject: BNSS
question: When shall the prosecutor and the accused be allowed to recall the witnesses?
options: the court has to explain the charge to the accused
when a charge is altered or added by the court
in all of the above conditions
explanation: The specific right to recall witnesses under Section 240 is triggered when the Court alters or adds to any charge after the trial starts.

subject: BNSS
question: Which provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 empower a criminal court to recall/re-examine witnesses in a criminal case?
explanation: A court can recall witnesses under Section 240 (upon alteration of charge) and has general powers to recall material witnesses under Section 348 (old Section 311 CrPC).

subject: BNSS
question: "For every distinct offence of which any person is accused, there shall be a separate charge and every such charge shall be tried separately", is provided in Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 under:-
explanation: Section 241 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 218 of the old CrPC) lays down the general rule of separate charges and separate trials for distinct offences.

subject: BNSS
question: A commits robbery on B, and in doing so voluntarily causes hurt to him. Whether A may be separately charged with offences under section 115, 309(4) and 309(6) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
options: In all said offences only with the consent of accused
In all said offences only upon application of prosecution
explanation: Under Section 243(1) of the BNSS (old Section 220(1) CrPC), if a series of acts form the same transaction, the accused may be charged with and tried at one trial for every such offence.

subject: BNSS
question: When a person is accused of more offences than one...........committed within the space of twelve months, he may be charged with and tried at one trial for any number of them not exceeding five.
explanation: Section 242(1) of the BNSS (corresponding to Section 219 CrPC) governs the trial of joint offences of the "same kind" committed within a year.

subject: BNSS
question: Offence of same kind committed, by a person accused of more than one offences within the space of twelve months, whether in respect of the same person or not, may be charged with and tried at one trial under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for how many offences?
explanation: Under Section 242(1) of the BNSS, the maximum number of offences of the same kind that can be tried together in a single trial is **five** (a change from the limit of three under the old CrPC).

subject: BNSS
question: ...........offences of same kind within 12 months can be charged together as per the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
explanation: Section 242 of the BNSS allows up to five offences of the same kind to be tried together.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 242 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, 'offence of same kind' means:-
options: when they are punishable with the same amount of punishment
when they are punishable under same section
when they are punishable with the same amount of punishment under the same section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 or of any special or local law
explanation: Under Section 242(2), offences are of the same kind when they are punishable with the same amount of punishment under the same section of the BNS or any special/local law.

subject: BNSS
question: If a series of acts are so connected together as to form the same transaction, and more than one offence is committed by the same person:-
options: He shall be charged and tried separately for every such offence
He shall be charged with every such offence and tried at one trial for all the offences.
Some of the offences may be clubbed and tried at one trial.
explanation: Under Section 243(1) of the BNSS (old Section 220(1) CrPC), the accused can be charged and tried at one trial for all offences committed in the same transaction.

subject: BNSS
question:
With reference to the 'Charge' which of the statement is/are correct?
(1) Every charge under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 states the offences with which the accused may be charged.
(2) If in the course of same transaction, more offences than one are committed by the same person, he can be charged at one trial.
explanation: Both statements are correct: a charge must state the offence, and multiple offences in the same transaction can be tried together.

subject: BNSS
question: 'A' is accused of an act which may amount to Criminal Breach of Trust or Cheating. He is only charged with Cheating, but it appears in evidence that he committed the offence of Criminal Breach of Trust. Under Section 244 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, he may be:-
options: Acquitted from the charge of Criminal Breach of Trust
Convicted of Criminal Breach of Trust
Discharged from the charge of Criminal Breach of Trust
explanation: Section 244 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 221 of the old CrPC) provides that if the accused is charged with one offence, but the evidence shows he committed a different offence for which he could have been charged, he may be convicted of the offence proved, even if not charged with it.

subject: BNSS
question: 'A' is accused of an act which may amount to theft, receiving stolen property, or criminal breach of trust. He is charged only with 'theft'. If the evidence reveals that he committed the offence of criminal breach of trust, what is the legal consequence under the BNSS, 2023?
options: He may be convicted of criminal breach of trust, though he was not charged with it
He may not be convicted of criminal breach of trust because he was not charged with it
He can neither be convicted of theft nor of criminal breach of trust
He may only be convicted of theft because he was charged with theft
explanation: Under Section 244 of the BNSS, 2023, when there is doubt as to which offence the facts will prove, and the accused is charged with only one of them, he can be convicted of the other offence if proved by evidence.

subject: BNSS
question: 'A' is charged with the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of a dangerous weapon under Section 118(2) of the BNS, 2023. The prosecution fails to prove that a dangerous weapon was used. However, the accused shows that he acted on grave and sudden provocation. Under Section 245 of the BNSS, 2023, the accused:-
options: May be held guilty of voluntarily causing grievous hurt on provocation under Section 122(2) of the BNS, 2023, even though no charge for the said offence was framed
Must be acquitted since no charge for any other offence has been framed
explanation: Section 245 of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 222 CrPC) allows conviction for a minor offence when the major offence charged is not proved but the facts prove the minor offence.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is the joint trial of several persons permissible?
explanation: Section 246 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 223 of the old CrPC) provides the statutory guidelines for the joint trial of several accused persons under specified circumstances.

subject: BNSS
question: For every distinct offence of which any person is accused, there shall be a separate charge. Which of the following sections contain the statutory exceptions to this rule under the BNSS, 2023?
explanation: The exceptions to the general rule of separate trials for distinct offences (Section 241) are contained in Sections 242, 243, 244, and 246 of the BNSS, 2023.

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following ranges of sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is the procedure for Sessions Trial provided?
explanation: Chapter XIX of the BNSS, 2023 (comprising Sections 248 to 260) lays down the procedure to be followed in trials before a Court of Session.

subject: BNSS
question: The procedure for trial before the Court of Session is dealt with in which Section range of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Sections 248 to 260 of the BNSS, 2023 dictate the stages of a Sessions Court trial, from the opening of the case to the final judgment.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 248 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, in every trial before a Court of Session, the prosecution shall be conducted by:-
explanation: Section 248 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 225 of the old CrPC) mandates that the prosecution in a Sessions trial must be conducted by a Public Prosecutor.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the recording of reasons by a Court under the BNSS, 2023?
options: When a complaint is dismissed, the court shall record the reasons
When an accused is discharged, the court need not record the reasons
When a charge is framed the court need not record the reasons
When cognizance is taken of an offence, the court need not record the reasons
explanation: Under Section 250 of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 227 CrPC), the Judge must record his reasons for discharging the accused. Thus, stating the court 'need not record' reasons for discharge is incorrect.

subject: BNSS
question: In a criminal proceeding, the 'Charge' is framed by:-
explanation: Framing of the charge is a judicial act performed by the Court (under Section 251 BNSS/Section 228 CrPC for Sessions, and corresponding sections for warrant cases) after considering the record and documents.

subject: BNSS
question: At the stage of framing a charge, the Court is required to:-
options: determine whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused
determine whether there is a ground for conviction of the accused
consider the evidence produced by the accused
explanation: At the stage of framing a charge under Section 251 of the BNSS, the court only needs to evaluate whether there is a prima facie case and a 'sufficient ground for proceeding', not whether the material is sufficient for conviction.

subject: BNSS
question: If at the stage of framing of charge, the Sessions Court finds that the case is not exclusively triable by it, it may:-
options: Send the case to the Chief Judicial Magistrate for framing of the charge
Frame the charge and transfer the case to the Chief Judicial Magistrate, or any other Judicial Magistrate of the first class
Frame the charge and transfer the case to a Magistrate of the second class
Send the case to Lok Adalat
explanation: Under Section 251(1)(a) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 228(1)(a) CrPC), if the case is not exclusively triable by the Court of Session, it may frame a charge and transfer the case to the CJM or any other JMFC.

subject: BNSS
question: During a Sessions trial, under which section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 may the Sessions Judge order the acquittal of the accused before pronouncing judgment, if there is no evidence?
explanation: Section 255 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 232 of the old CrPC) provides that if, after taking the prosecution evidence, the Judge considers that there is no evidence that the accused committed the offence, the Judge shall record an order of acquittal.

subject: BNSS
question: Under what circumstance does a Judge record an order of acquittal under Section 255 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
options: If he finds that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding with the trial
If he finds that there is no evidence that the accused committed the offence
If the accused pleads 'not guilty' and the prosecution does not contest that
In all of the above cases
explanation: An acquittal under Section 255 of the BNSS is recorded specifically when, after the prosecution's case is closed and the accused is examined, the Judge concludes there is no evidence linking the accused to the offence.

subject: BNSS
question: If the accused is not acquitted under Section 255 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the Court shall call upon him to enter on:-
explanation: Under Section 256(1) of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 233(1) of the old CrPC), if the accused is not acquitted, he must be called upon to enter on his defence and produce his evidence.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which of the following provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 can the accused file a written statement in support of his defence during a Sessions trial?
explanation: Section 256(2) of the BNSS, 2023 explicitly allows the accused to put in any written statement in support of his defence, which the Judge must file with the record.

subject: BNSS
question: Section 257 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 makes provision for:-
explanation: Section 257 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 234 of the old CrPC) provides that when the examination of the defence witnesses is complete, the prosecutor shall sum up his case and the accused shall be entitled to reply (Arguments stage).

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following orders can be passed by the Sessions Judge under Section 258 of the BNSS, 2023, after the trial of a case is completed?
options: Either an order of acquittal or conviction
explanation: Section 258 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 235 of the old CrPC) provides that after hearing arguments, the Judge shall deliver a judgment of acquittal or conviction.

subject: BNSS
question: Section 259 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 lays down a special procedure regarding liability to enhanced punishment in consequence of a previous conviction. This section is applicable to trials before:-
explanation: Section 259 of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 236 CrPC) applies specifically to trials before a Court of Session, where the accused is charged with a previous conviction and does not admit it.

subject: BNSS
question: Trial of warrant cases by Magistrates is dealt with in which Section range of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Chapter XX of the BNSS, 2023 (comprising Sections 261 to 273) details the procedure for the trial of warrant-cases by Magistrates, divided into cases instituted on a police report and cases instituted otherwise.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following sections of the BNSS, 2023 dictates when an accused shall be discharged by a Magistrate in a warrant-case instituted on a police report?
options: Section 262 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 287 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 376 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 281 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Section 262 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 239 of the old CrPC) provides that the Magistrate shall discharge the accused if he considers the charge against the accused to be groundless.

subject: BNSS
question: As per Section 262 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, what can the Magistrate consider while deciding whether to discharge the accused?
options: The charge-sheet and its accompanying documents only
The documents produced by the accused also
The documents collected from the accused during investigation, but produced on application by him
Discharge of an accused summoned vide Section 358 of the BNSS, 2023
explanation: At the stage of discharge under Section 262, the Magistrate considers the police report and documents sent under Section 193. The accused is not entitled to produce his defense documents at this stage.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the recording of reasons in a warrant-case before a Magistrate?
options: When a complaint is dismissed, the court shall record the reasons
When an accused is discharged, the court need not record the reasons
When a charge is framed the court need not record the reasons
When cognizance is taken of an offence, the court need not record the reasons
explanation: Under Section 262 of the BNSS, 2023, if the Magistrate discharges the accused, he must record his reasons for doing so. Thus, stating the court 'need not record' reasons is incorrect.

subject: BNSS
question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, in a warrant-case instituted on a police report, when does the trial actually commence?
explanation: In a warrant-case instituted on a police report, the trial begins when the charge is framed by the Magistrate. Prior proceedings belong to the pre-trial stage.

subject: BNSS
question: A charge is framed by the Magistrate in a warrant-case on the basis of:-
options: Police report and documents sent with it
Documents produced by the prosecution as well as the accused
explanation: Section 263 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 240 of the old CrPC) provides that the charge is framed after considering the police report and documents sent under Section 193.

subject: BNSS
question: Which one of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 deals with 'evidence for defence' in a warrant-case tried by a Magistrate?
explanation: Section 266 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 243 of the old CrPC) governs the stage where the accused is called upon to enter his defence and produce his evidence.

subject: BNSS
question: In a trial on the charge of attempt to rape, at the stage of recording the evidence of the sixteen-year-old prosecutrix, the accused insists on being present and allowed to confront her by showing video-footage on his mobile phone. What is the correct legal position?
options: The request of the accused cannot be declined since the charge is only of an attempt to rape
The request of the accused cannot be declined since the prosecutrix is a child
The request of the accused may be declined, though the Court must adopt appropriate measures to ensure no direct confrontation between the accused and the prosecutrix
The request of the accused may be declined since the video-footage was not disclosed at any earlier stage
explanation: In cases of sexual offences, particularly involving minors, the court must protect the victim from direct face-to-face confrontation with the accused while ensuring the right of cross-examination is preserved through screens or video-conferencing.

subject: BNSS
question: When, in any warrant case instituted otherwise than on a police report, the accused appears or is brought before a Magistrate, the Magistrate shall:-
options: satisfy himself that he has complied with the provisions of Section 230 of the BNSS, 2023
postpone issue of process against the accused if he is residing at a place beyond his jurisdiction
either inquire into the case himself or direct an investigation by a police officer
proceed to hear the prosecution and take all such evidence as may be produced in support of the prosecution
explanation: Under Section 267 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 244 of the old CrPC), in cases instituted otherwise than on a police report, the Magistrate proceeds to hear the prosecution and record all prosecution evidence first.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following orders can be passed by the Magistrate under Section 271 of the BNSS, 2023 after the trial of a warrant case is completed?
options: Either an order of acquittal or conviction
explanation: Section 271 of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 248 CrPC) provides that after hearing the case, the Magistrate shall record an order of acquittal if the accused is not guilty, or find him guilty and pass sentence.

subject: BNSS
question: Hearing on sentence by a Magistrate is required, on conviction:-
options: in a summons trial case under Section 278(2) of B.N.S.S.
in a warrant trial case under Section 271(2) of B.N.S.S.
explanation: A hearing on the question of sentence is mandatory in warrant trials under Section 271(2) of the BNSS, 2023, whereas it is not a statutory requirement in summons trials.

subject: BNSS
question: In the case of State of Rajasthan vs. Love Kush Meena, the Supreme Court of India held that a mere fact of acquittal will not suffice for employment if it depends on whether the acquittal was 'clean' or on 'benefit of doubt', while relying on which of the following cases?
options: Avtar Singh vs. Union of India & Ors.
Sudha Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr.
Achhar Singh vs. State of Himachal Pradesh
Shaik Ahmed vs. State of Telangana
explanation: In State of Rajasthan v. Love Kush Meena (2021), the Supreme Court relied on the landmark judgment of Avtar Singh v. Union of India (2016) regarding verification of character and antecedents for public employment in cases of acquittal.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following sections of the BNSS, 2023 deals with the absence of the complainant during the trial of a warrant case?
options: Section 258 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 287 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 272 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 265 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Section 272 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 249 of the old CrPC) governs the discharge of the accused due to the absence of the complainant in complaint-instituted warrant cases.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 272 of the BNSS, 2023, when may the Magistrate, in his discretion, discharge the accused due to the absence of the complainant?
options: At any time before the charge has been framed and the complainant is absent on any day fixed for the hearing of the case
Offence is lawfully compounded or is not a cognizable offence
Both at any time before the charge has been framed and the complainant is absent on any day fixed for the hearing of the case and offence is lawfully compounded or is not a cognizable offence
At any time after the charge has been framed with respect to cognizable and compoundable offence
explanation: Section 272 allows discharge only if the complainant is absent before the charge is framed, and the offence is either non-cognizable or lawfully compoundable.

subject: BNSS
question: If the complainant is absent on the day fixed for the hearing of the warrant case, the Magistrate may discharge the accused if:-
options: The proceedings have been instituted upon complaint
The offence is non-cognizable or compoundable
The charge has not been framed
explanation: All three conditions: complaint-based case, non-cognizable or compoundable offence, and pre-charge stage must be met for a Magistrate to discharge the accused under Section 272.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 272 of the BNSS, 2023, in which of the following circumstances can the accused NOT be discharged due to the absence of the complainant?
options: When the charge has been framed
When the proceedings have been instituted on complaint
explanation: Once a charge is framed in a warrant-case, the Magistrate cannot discharge the accused under Section 272. He must proceed with the trial to its logical conclusion (acquittal or conviction).

subject: BNSS
question: What is incorrect regarding the power of a Magistrate to discharge the accused if the complainant is absent on the date of hearing?
options: It can be done before the charge has been framed
The provision would be applicable for complaint case and police case both
explanation: Discharge due to the absence of the complainant (Section 272) applies exclusively to cases instituted upon a private complaint, not to cases instituted on a police report.

subject: BNSS
question: What is the maximum amount of compensation that a Magistrate can direct the complainant or informant to pay for making an accusation without reasonable cause under Section 273 of the BNSS, 2023?
options: as he may determine but not exceeding the amount of fine he is empowered to impose
not exceeding the amount of fine he is empowered to impose for the particular offence for which accusation was made without reasonable cause
explanation: Section 273 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 250 of the old CrPC) provides that the Magistrate can award compensation up to the limit of the fine he is empowered to impose under the Sanhita.

subject: BNSS
question: The procedure for the trial of summons cases by Magistrates is provided in which Section range of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Chapter XXI of the BNSS, 2023 (comprising Sections 274 to 282) governs the trial of summons-cases by Magistrates.

subject: BNSS
question: Provision for the discharge of an accused in a trial of a summons case by a Magistrate is provided in:-
explanation: There is no concept or statutory provision of 'discharge' of an accused in a summons-case trial. The Magistrate must either convict or acquit the accused.

subject: BNSS
question: In the trial of a summons case by a Magistrate:-
options: Charges can be framed provided the accused does not object
Only substance of accusation is to be stated
explanation: Under Section 274 of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 251 CrPC), it is not necessary to frame a formal charge in a summons case; only the particulars of the offence (substance of accusation) must be stated to the accused.

subject: BNSS
question: In a summons case, when the accused appears or is brought before the Magistrate, it shall NOT be necessary to:-
options: State the particulars of the offence of which he is accused
Ask whether he has any defence to make
explanation: Under Section 274 of the BNSS, 2023, while the substance of the accusation must be stated, framing a formal charge is explicitly dispensed with.

subject: BNSS
question: Framing of a formal charge shall not be necessary in:-
options: trial of warrant-case instituted on a Police report by a Magistrate
trial of summons case by a Magistrate
trial before a Court of Session
trial of warrant-case instituted other than a Police report by a Magistrate
explanation: A formal charge is mandatory in Sessions trials and both types of warrant-case trials, but is not required in summons-case trials.

subject: BNSS
question: When in a summons-case the accused appears or is brought before the Magistrate:-
options: the prosecutor shall open his case by describing the charge
the Magistrate shall frame in writing a charge against the accused if there is ground for presuming he committed the offence
the particulars of the offence shall be stated to him, and he shall be asked whether he pleads guilty or has any defence to make, but it shall not be necessary to frame a formal charge
explanation: This maps directly to Section 274 of the BNSS, 2023, establishing the initial procedure when the accused appears in a summons case.

subject: BNSS
