question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding a Magistrate trying a summons case?
options: shall frame charge after hearing the accused and the prosecution
may discharge the accused after hearing the prosecution and the accused
shall not hear the accused and simply particulars of the offence shall be stated to him
explanation: Under Section 274 of the BNSS, 2023, the Magistrate simply states the particulars of the offence and asks for a plea, without conducting a pre-charge hearing of the accused.

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following trials is a hearing of the accused on the question of sentence not necessary?
options: Trial before a Court of Session
explanation: A hearing on sentence is required in Sessions trials and warrant trials, but there is no such requirement for summons trials under Chapter XXI of the BNSS.

subject: BNSS
question: In reference to the trial of summons cases by a Magistrate, which of the following statements is correct?
options: The Court shall frame charge after hearing the accused and the prosecution
The Court may discharge the accused after hearing the prosecution and the accused
There is no requirement for the Court to hear the accused on the question of sentence
explanation: Since summons cases are for minor offences, the law dispenses with both formal charge-framing and the separate hearing stage for sentencing.

subject: BNSS
question:
As per the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which of the following disposals result in an acquittal of the accused?
A. Disposal under Section 279
B. Disposal under Section 268(2)
C. Disposal under Section 226
D. Disposal under Section 359
explanation: Disposal under Section 279 (non-appearance or death of complainant in summons cases) and Section 359 (withdrawal from prosecution under old Section 321 CrPC) amount to an acquittal.

subject: BNSS
question: If an application filed for the withdrawal of a complaint under Section 280 of the BNSS, 2023 is allowed, the accused will be:-
explanation: Section 280 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 257 of the old CrPC) states that if the Magistrate permits the withdrawal of the complaint, he shall acquit the accused.

subject: BNSS
question: If a complaint is withdrawn under Section 280 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the Magistrate shall:-
options: acquit the accused after the charge has been framed and discharge before the charge has been framed
explanation: The statutory effect of allowing the withdrawal of a complaint in a summons case is always the acquittal of the accused, regardless of the stage of the trial.

subject: BNSS
question: Withdrawal of a complaint under Chapter XXI of the BNSS, 2023 results in the:-
options: discharge of the accused in cases where the charge has not yet been framed
acquittal of the accused in cases where charge has already been framed
acquittal of the accused irrespective of whether the charge has been framed or not
explanation: Since formal charges are not framed in summons trials, withdrawal of the complaint under Section 280 always leads to the acquittal of the accused.

subject: BNSS
question: Withdrawal of the complaint in a Summons case under Section 280 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 results in:-
options: acquittal or discharge depending on the stage at which the withdrawal is permitted
acquittal after charge has been framed and discharge before charge has been framed
explanation: Section 280 explicitly mandates that the Magistrate 'shall acquit the accused' upon permitting the withdrawal of the complaint.

subject: BNSS
question: Stoppage of proceedings in a criminal case under Section 281 of the BNSS, 2023 has the effect of:-
options: acquittal where the evidence of the principal witness has been recorded
discharge in all other cases where the evidence of the principal witness has not been recorded
explanation: Under Section 281 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 258 of the old CrPC), stopping proceedings has the effect of an acquittal if the principal witness's evidence is recorded; otherwise, it has the effect of a discharge.

subject: BNSS
question: Proceedings under Section 281 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 can be stopped:-
options: in a summons case instituted upon a complaint
in a warrant case instituted upon a complaint
in a summons case instituted otherwise than upon a complaint
in a cognizable warrant case instituted otherwise than upon a complaint
explanation: The power to stop proceedings under Section 281 (old Section 258 CrPC) applies only to summons cases instituted otherwise than upon a complaint (i.e., police report cases).

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following cases may a Chief Judicial Magistrate stop the proceedings at any stage without pronouncing any judgment under Section 281 of the BNSS, 2023?
options: warrant case instituted otherwise than upon a complaint
warrant case instituted on a police report
summons case instituted otherwise than upon complaint
summons case instituted otherwise than a police report
explanation: Only in summons cases instituted otherwise than upon complaint (i.e. on a police report or suo motu) can the CJM or any other JMFC stop proceedings under Section 281.

subject: BNSS
question: By which section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 can the Court convert summons cases into warrant cases?
explanation: Section 282 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 259 of the old CrPC) provides the power to try a summons case as a warrant case under certain conditions.

subject: BNSS
question: The power of a court to convert a summons case into a warrant case is provided under which provision of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 282 contains the statutory procedure allowing conversion in the interest of justice.

subject: BNSS
question: In which section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 can a criminal trial court pass an order to try a summons case as a warrant case in the 'interest of justice'?
explanation: Section 282 empowers the Magistrate, in the interest of justice, to try a summons case as a warrant case if the offence is punishable with imprisonment exceeding six months.

subject: BNSS
question: In the interest of justice, a Magistrate has the power to try a summons case as a warrant case, provided the offence is punishable with imprisonment exceeding:-
explanation: Under Section 282 of the BNSS, 2023, conversion is only permissible if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding six months.

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following circumstances does a Magistrate have the power to convert summons cases into warrant cases?
explanation: The conversion under Section 282 must be done specifically if the Magistrate is of the opinion that it is 'in the interest of justice'.

subject: BNSS
question: During the trial of a case involving accusations of medical negligence resulting in the death of a human being, after having recorded the evidence of the complainant and some other witnesses, the criminal court is of the view that the offence should have been tried in accordance with the procedure for a warrant-case. What is the correct procedure?
options: The Court may convert the case into a warrant-case and continue recording of remaining evidence
The Court cannot convert the case into a warrant-case since the trial has begun and cannot be stopped
The Court cannot convert the case into a warrant-case since it would lead to the case being re-heard

The Court may convert the case into a warrant-case, but must first frame a formal charge and, after recording the plea of the accused, take evidence for the prosecution by recalling the witnesses earlier examined
explanation: When a case is converted from a summons case to a warrant case, the court must rehear the witnesses examined earlier and frame a formal charge as required by warrant-case procedure.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is the provision regarding 'summary trial' given?
explanation: Chapter XXII of the BNSS, 2023 (comprising Sections 283 to 288) sets out the rules and procedures for summary trials by Magistrates.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following courts may summarily try offences mentioned in Section 283 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Under Section 283(1) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 260(1) CrPC), the CJM, Metropolitan Magistrate, or any JMFC specially empowered by the High Court can conduct summary trials.

subject: BNSS
question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, who empowers a Judicial Magistrate First Class to conduct summary trials?
explanation: Under Section 283(1)(c) of the BNSS, 2023, any Magistrate of the first class must be specially empowered in this behalf by the High Court. (The book answer key lists option D).

subject: BNSS
question: A Magistrate of the first class, specially empowered, shall try in a summary way which of the following offences under Section 283 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
options: Theft under Section 303(2), 305 or 306 of the BNS, 2023 where the value of the property stolen does not exceed twenty thousand rupees
Offences under Section 331(2) and (3) of the BNS, 2023 (Lurking house-trespass)
Receiving or retaining stolen property under Section 317(2) of the BNS, 2023 where the value does not exceed twenty thousand rupees
explanation: Section 283(1) of the BNSS, 2023 allows summary trials for various minor offences, including theft, receiving stolen property (both where value is ≤ 20,000 rupees), and house-trespass.

subject: BNSS
question: Which one of the following offences is triable summarily under the BNSS, 2023?
options: insult with intent to provoke a breach of the peace under Section 352, and criminal intimidation under Section 351 of the BNS, 2023
explanation: Section 283(1) explicitly lists offences under Section 352 (insult to provoke breach of peace) and Section 351 (criminal intimidation) of the BNS as summarily triable.

subject: BNSS
question: Which one of the following offences shall NOT be tried summarily under Chapter XXII of the BNSS, 2023?
options: Offences punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding three years
Offences under Section 331(2) and (3) of the BNS, 2023
Theft under Section 303(2), 305 or 306 of the BNS, 2023 where the value of the property stolen does not exceed twenty thousand rupees
explanation: Under Section 283(1)(i), summary trial is restricted to offences not punishable with death, imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term exceeding two years. Under BNSS, some offenses are updated, but the general threshold is that serious offenses exceeding three years (or two years generally) are not triable summarily.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following offences cannot be summarily tried by a Magistrate?
options: Theft when the value of stolen property is below Rs. 20,000
Offences relating to Section 331(2) and (3) of the BNS, 2023
Offence of abetment of the offences enumerated under Section 283(vi) of the BNSS, 2023
explanation: Grievous hurt is a serious offence punishable with up to 7 years imprisonment (under BNS Section 117) and is therefore not triable summarily under Section 283 of the BNSS.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following offences is not triable summarily under Section 283 of the BNSS, 2023?
options: Theft where the value of the property stolen does not exceed Rs. 20,000
Assisting in the concealment of stolen property of the value not exceeding Rs. 20,000
Receiving or retaining stolen property under Section 317(2) of the BNS, 2023, where the value of the property does not exceed Rs. 20,000
explanation: Lurking house trespass (without other qualifiers) is a serious offence. The book answer key lists option B as not triable summarily.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 283 of the BNSS, 2023, the Magistrate may, after giving the accused a reasonable opportunity of being heard, try in a summary way all or any of the offences not punishable with death or imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term exceeding:-
explanation: Section 283(1) of the BNSS, 2023 allows the Magistrate to try summarily offences not punishable with death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment for a term exceeding three years.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 can a Magistrate of the second class conduct a summary trial?
explanation: Section 284 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 261 of the old CrPC) provides that the High Court may empower any Magistrate of the second class to try summarily any offence punishable only with fine or with imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Chapter XXII of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, what is the maximum sentence of imprisonment which can be imposed for an offence tried in a summary trial?
explanation: Section 285(2) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 262(2) CrPC) mandates that no sentence of imprisonment for a term exceeding three months shall be passed in the case of any conviction under this Chapter.

subject: BNSS
question: In a summary trial, the maximum sentence of imprisonment that can be awarded is:-
explanation: The maximum term of imprisonment that can be passed under summary trial procedure is strictly limited to three months by Section 285(2).

subject: BNSS
question: Out of the following statements, which one is incorrect regarding the trial of summons and warrant cases under summary trial?
options: Summons case procedure shall be followed while trying summons case
Warrant case procedure shall be followed while trying warrant case
Summons case procedure shall be followed while trying warrant case in a summary way
Warrant case procedure shall be followed while trying warrant case in a summary way
explanation: Section 285(1) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 262(1) CrPC) provides that in summary trials, the procedure prescribed for summons-cases shall be followed, even if the case is a warrant case. Thus, statement D is incorrect.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following need NOT be a particular entered in the record of a summary trial under Section 286 of the BNSS, 2023?
options: The date on which proceedings terminated
explanation: Section 286 of the BNSS, 2023 lists the particulars to be entered in the record, which includes the parentage of the accused, but does not mandate the entry of the parentage of the complainant.

subject: BNSS
question: In which Chapter of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is the alternative dispute resolution mechanism of Plea Bargaining mentioned?
explanation: Chapter XXIII of the BNSS, 2023 (comprising Sections 289 to 300) contains the provisions regulating Plea Bargaining.

subject: BNSS
question: The right of an accused to plea bargain under Indian law is restricted to:-
explanation: Plea bargaining in India is primarily 'sentence bargaining', which allows the accused to plead guilty in exchange for a lesser sentence or release on probation.

subject: BNSS
question: Plea bargaining under Indian law implies:-
options: bargain for declaration that the accused is innocent
bargain for dilution of the charge
bargaining for lesser punishment or release on probation on accepting the charge
plea for lesser punishment and dilution of the charge
explanation: Under Chapter XXIII, plea bargaining enables an accused to work out a mutually satisfactory disposition, including receiving a reduced sentence or probation, on admitting guilt.

subject: BNSS
question: For the purpose of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, 'Plea bargaining' is applicable to:-
explanation: Section 289(1) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 265A CrPC) makes plea bargaining applicable to both cases instituted on a police report and cases instituted on a private complaint.

subject: BNSS
question: The provisions of plea bargaining under the BNSS, 2023 are applicable:-
options: where the punishment is for more than 7 years imprisonment
after issuance of process under Section 227
explanation: Plea bargaining can only be applied for after the Magistrate has issued process and the charge-sheet/complaint is pending trial, and is excluded for juveniles, appellate stages, and offences exceeding 7 years.

subject: BNSS
question: Plea bargaining is applicable to offences other than those for which the punishment of death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term exceeding........... has been provided.
explanation: Under Section 289(1), plea bargaining is not available for offences carrying sentences exceeding seven years of imprisonment.

subject: BNSS
question: Plea Bargaining is applicable to the offences punishable up to........... imprisonment.
explanation: The maximum threshold of punishment for offences where plea bargaining is permissible is seven years.

subject: BNSS
question: The doctrine of Plea bargaining is NOT applicable to an offence punishable with:-
explanation: Plea bargaining is barred for offences punishable with death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment exceeding 7 years.

subject: BNSS
question: The provisions of Chapter XXIII of the BNSS, 2023 on Plea Bargaining are not applicable to cases where the final report discloses:-
options: offences punishable with imprisonment for life
explanation: Plea bargaining is strictly barred for both capital punishment cases (death) and life imprisonment cases.

subject: BNSS
question: The provisions of 'Plea-Bargaining' under Chapter XXIII of the BNSS, 2023 are not applicable if the offence is committed against a child below the age of:-
explanation: Under Section 289(2) of the BNSS, 2023, plea bargaining is barred if the offence is committed against a child (which is defined as a person below the age of eighteen years).

subject: BNSS
question: An accused may apply for plea bargaining under Chapter XXIII of the BNSS, 2023, unless he has committed:-
options: an offence for which the punishment extends to imprisonment exceeding seven years
an offence which affects the socio-economic condition of the country
explanation: Section 289 of the BNSS excludes cases where the offence exceeds 7 years, affects the socio-economic conditions of the country, or is committed against a woman.

subject: BNSS
question: An accused can make an application for plea bargaining in the Court in which the offence is pending trial, except when he is alleged to have committed:-
options: an offence affecting the socio-economic condition of the country
explanation: Offences affecting the socio-economic condition of the country are specifically excluded from the scope of plea bargaining under Section 289.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following statements is true with respect to Chapter XXIII of the BNSS, 2023 on Plea Bargaining?
options: It does not apply where such offences have been committed against a child below the age of eighteen years
It does not apply where such offences have been committed against women
It does not apply where such offences are punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding seven years
explanation: Plea bargaining is not applicable when the offence is committed against a child under 18, against a woman, or when the punishment exceeds 7 years. The book answer key lists option D.

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following cases can a plea bargain NOT be effected?
options: where the offence is punishable with imprisonment exceeding 7 years
where the offence is against a child
where the offence is against a woman
explanation: Plea bargaining is strictly disallowed in all the listed scenarios under Section 289.

subject: BNSS
question: Provisions relating to 'plea bargaining' are applicable to:-
options: offences affecting socio-economic conditions of India
explanation: Since all options A, B, and C represent statutory exclusions to plea bargaining under Section 289, the provisions are applicable to none of them (Option D).

subject: BNSS
question: The offences affecting the socio-economic condition of the country, for which plea bargaining is not applicable, shall be determined and notified by:-
explanation: Under Section 289(2) of the BNSS, 2023, the Central Government is the authorized body to determine and notify the socio-economic offences excluded from plea bargaining.

subject: BNSS
question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, an application for plea bargaining can be filed by:-
explanation: Under Section 290(1) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 265B CrPC), only the accused person is empowered to file an application for plea bargaining.

subject: BNSS
question: An application for Plea bargaining may be filed by:-
explanation: Plea bargaining is a voluntary option exercised solely by the accused to plead guilty in exchange for concessions.

subject: BNSS
question: A person accused of an offence may file an application for plea bargaining within a period of........... from the date of framing of charge:-
explanation: Section 290(1) of the BNSS, 2023 contains a new timeline: the accused must file the plea bargaining application within thirty days from the date of framing of charge.

subject: BNSS
question: A person accused of an offence may apply for a plea bargaining:-
options: In the Court in which his case is pending trial
explanation: Section 290(1) mandates that the application containing the brief description of the case and affidavit must be filed in the Court in which the offence is pending trial.

subject: BNSS
question: The Court shall examine the accused on receiving an application for plea bargaining to satisfy itself that the application is made voluntarily, which must be conducted:-
explanation: Section 290(4) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 265B(4) CrPC) requires the Court to examine the accused in camera (in the absence of other parties) to ensure the application is voluntary.

subject: BNSS
question: The examination of the accused by the Court under Section 290(4) of the BNSS, 2023 to verify the voluntariness of the plea bargaining application must be done:-
options: in open court in the presence of the Public Prosecutor
in camera in the absence of the other party to the case
in open court in the presence of the victim
explanation: An in-camera examination prevents coercion and ensures the accused is acting of his own free will without pressure from the prosecution or victim.

subject: BNSS
question: Who can participate in the meeting for working out a mutually satisfactory disposition under Section 290 of the BNSS, 2023?
options: The accused, victim, Public Prosecutor, and the investigating officer
explanation: Under Section 290(4)(a), the Court issues notice to the Public Prosecutor, investigating officer, and the victim to participate in a meeting to work out a satisfactory disposition.

subject: BNSS
question: Guidelines for working out a mutually satisfactory disposition of the case are covered under which Section of the BNSS, 2023?
explanation: Section 291 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 265C of the old CrPC) prescribes the guidelines to be followed by the court and parties while working out a mutually satisfactory disposition.

subject: BNSS
question:
Evaluate the correctness of the following statement regarding plea bargaining:
"Under the provisions for Plea-bargaining in the Sanhita, in a case instituted otherwise than on a police report, the mutually satisfactory disposition is a matter exclusively between the complainant on one hand and the accused on the other."
options: The above statement is incorrect since the victim is entitled to be called and participate in the meeting convened for the purpose.
The above statement is correct since the complainant has the prerogative to withdraw the case.
The above statement is correct since the procedure is in the discretion of the Court.
The above statement is correct since complainant always represents the interest of the victim.
explanation: Section 291(b) ensures that in a complaint case, the meeting involves the accused and the victim (or complainant), but other guidelines and the Court's supervision are mandatory, making the 'exclusive' statement incorrect. The book answer key lists option A.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 293 of the BNSS, 2023, where a satisfactory disposition has been worked out, what can the Court do?
options: Must award compensation whether or not agreed by the parties
Cannot award any punishment since that would be against the spirit of amicable settlement
explanation: Under Section 293 (old Section 265E CrPC), the Court awards compensation as agreed by the parties, and then passes a sentence (which can be a fraction of the minimum or maximum punishment, or release on probation), so both A and B are incorrect statements. The book answer key lists option D.

subject: BNSS
question: Upon working out a mutually satisfactory disposition of the case, the Court shall deliver its judgment under Section 294 of the BNSS, 2023:-
options: by transmitting it to the jail authorities
explanation: Section 294 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 265F of the old CrPC) provides that the Court shall deliver its judgment in the open court.

subject: BNSS
question: The statements or facts stated by an accused in an application for plea bargaining under Chapter XXIII of the BNSS, 2023:-
options: can be used in any other case against the accused
can be used in any other case against the accused only with the permission of the Court
cannot be used for any other purpose except for the purpose of plea bargaining
can be used for any other purpose
explanation: Section 299 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 265K of the old CrPC) provides that statements or facts stated by the accused in a plea bargaining application shall not be used for any other purpose.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following is NOT expressly included in the definition of 'prison' under Section 301 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
options: Subsidiary jail declared to be so by general or special order
explanation: Section 301 of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 266 CrPC) defines 'prison' to include reformatories, Borstal institutions, and subsidiary jails, but explicitly excludes a police lock-up from this definition.

subject: BNSS
question: Where the defendant is confined in a prison, the summons shall be delivered or sent to:-
options: the officer in charge of the prison for service on defendant
explanation: Under Section 302 of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 267 CrPC), if a person is confined in a prison, the summons must be served through the officer in charge of the prison.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which section of law does a Magistrate have the power to issue a 'commission' for the examination of a witness in prison?
explanation: Section 306 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 271 of the old CrPC) provides that the provisions of this Chapter shall be without prejudice to the power of the Court to issue a commission under Section 318.

subject: BNSS
question: For the purpose of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, who may determine the language of each Court in the State other than the High Court?
options: The High Court of the State
The Legislative Assembly of the State
explanation: Section 307 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 272 of the old CrPC) provides that the State Government may determine what shall be the language of each Court within the State other than the High Court.

subject: BNSS
question: If a trial Court records the evidence of witnesses in a case where the accused is in custody, without ensuring his presence in the court (either physically or electronically), which of the following statements is correct?
options: The judgment passed by the trial Court in such proceedings would be vitiated by virtue of Section 308(1) of the B.N.S.S.
The judgment passed by the trial Court in such proceedings would be saved by virtue of Section 506 of the B.N.S.S.
The judgment passed by the trial Court in such proceedings would be saved by virtue of Section 511 of the B.N.S.S.
The judgment passed by the trial Court in such proceedings would be saved by virtue of Section 355 of the B.N.S.S.
explanation: Section 308(1) of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 273 CrPC) mandates that all evidence taken in the course of the trial or other proceedings shall be taken in the presence of the accused, or when his personal attendance is dispensed with, in the presence of his pleader. Failure to do so vitiates the trial.

subject: BNSS
question: The evidence of a Malayalam-speaking witness from Kerala, during a criminal trial in Delhi, is recorded in Malayalam with the help of a translator. The presiding judge is also from Kerala and knows the language. He dispenses with the requirement of translation of the deposition into the language of the court. What is the correct legal position?
options: The order of the presiding judge is correct as it is he who has to appreciate the evidence and decide the case
The order of the presiding judge is correct as it is a matter of his discretion
The order of the presiding judge is incorrect since it is mandatory for such translation to be prepared in the language of the court
The order of the presiding judge is incorrect since there may have been errors made in the Malayalam transcript
explanation: Under Section 312 of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 277 CrPC), if the evidence is given in a language other than the language of the court, a translation of the deposition into the language of the court must be prepared and filed as part of the record.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which provision of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 can the Court record the demeanour of a witness during examination?
explanation: Section 315 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 280 of the old CrPC) provides that when a presiding Judge or Magistrate has recorded the evidence of a witness, he shall also record such remarks (if any) as he thinks material respecting the demeanour of such witness.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which Section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is there a provision regarding the recording of remarks by a Magistrate respecting the demeanour of a witness?
explanation: Section 315 specifically deals with recording the demeanour of the witness under the BNSS, 2023.

subject: BNSS
question: The provisions of Section 316 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (record in examination of accused) shall NOT apply in the course of:-
options: Warrant trial cases instituted on a police report
Warrant trial cases instituted otherwise than on a police report
explanation: Section 316(5) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 281(5) CrPC) states that nothing in this section shall apply to the examination of an accused person in the course of a summary trial.

subject: BNSS
question: Which one of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is related to the rule that an 'Interpreter is bound to interpret truthfully'?
explanation: Section 317 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 282 of the old CrPC) provides that an interpreter shall be bound to interpret truthfully.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which of the following Sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is the issue of a commission for the examination of the President or the Vice President of India as a witness provided?
explanation: Section 319 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 284 of the old CrPC) provides that if the President or Vice-President of India is a witness, a commission shall be issued for their examination.

subject: BNSS
question: When a commission is to be issued for the examination of a witness who is within the territory to which the BNSS, 2023 applies, to whom shall such commission be directed?
options: The District Judge within whose jurisdiction the witness is to be found
The District Magistrate within whose jurisdiction the witness is to be found
The Chief Judicial Magistrate within whose jurisdiction the witness is to be found
The Executive Magistrate within whose jurisdiction the witness is to be found
explanation: Under Section 320(1) of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 285(1) of the old CrPC), the commission shall be directed to the Chief Judicial Magistrate within whose jurisdiction the witness is to be found.

subject: BNSS
question: The admissibility of reports of certain government scientific experts without calling them as witnesses is prescribed in which section of the BNSS, 2023?
explanation: Section 329 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 293 of the old CrPC) provides that reports of certain government scientific experts may be used as evidence in any inquiry, trial, or other proceeding under this Sanhita.

subject: BNSS
question: In a criminal trial, without producing the Chemical Examiner to the Government, the report given by him upon a thing duly submitted for analysis in the course of any proceeding under the BNSS, 2023:-
options: Can be used as evidence only in summons cases
Can be used only to refresh the memory of the investigating officer coming in evidence
explanation: Under Section 329(1), a report of a Chemical Examiner to Government may be used as evidence without calling him as a witness.

subject: BNSS
question: Section 329 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 regarding reports of government scientific experts applies to which of the following?
options: the Director of a Central or State Forensic Science Laboratory
the Deputy Director of a Central or State Forensic Science Laboratory
the Assistant Director of a Central or State Forensic Science Laboratory
explanation: Under Section 329(4) of the BNSS, 2023, the application of this section extends to Directors, Deputy Directors, and Assistant Directors of Central or State Forensic Science Laboratories.

subject: BNSS
question: Section 329 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 does not apply to which of the following Government Scientific Experts?
options: any Chemical Examiner or Assistant Chemical Examiner to Government
the Director of the Finger Print Bureau
State Examiner for the questioned documents
explanation: Section 329(4) specifies the experts (such as Chemical Examiners, Chief Controller of Explosives, Director of Finger Print Bureau). The book answer key lists option D.

subject: BNSS
question: The evidence of any person whose evidence is of a formal character which may be given by affidavit is provisioned in:-
options: Section 288 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 428 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 315 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 332 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Section 332 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 296 of the old CrPC) provides that the evidence of any person whose evidence is of a formal character may be given by affidavit.

subject: BNSS
question: The authorities under Section 333 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 before whom affidavits may be sworn or affirmed include:-
options: any Judge or any Judicial or Executive Magistrate
any Commissioner of Oaths appointed by a High Court or Court of Session
any notary appointed under the Notaries Act, 1952
explanation: Section 333 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 297 of the old CrPC) specifies that affidavits to be used before any Court may be sworn before any Judge, Magistrate, Commissioner of Oaths, or Notary.

subject: BNSS
question: The provisions for proving previous conviction are envisaged in which of the following Sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 334 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 298 of the old CrPC) lays down the modes of proving a previous conviction or acquittal in any inquiry or trial.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 can the examination of a witness be conducted in the absence of the accused?
explanation: Section 335 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 299 of the old CrPC) permits the deposition of witnesses to be recorded in the absence of the accused if the accused has absconded or if the offender is unknown.

subject: BNSS
question: Which Section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 provides for the admissibility of evidence of public servants, experts, and police officers in certain cases?
explanation: Section 336 is a newly added section in the BNSS, 2023, designed to allow depositions of public servants, scientific experts, or medical officers to be admitted in evidence if the officer is dead, cannot be found, or is incapable of giving evidence.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following is the correct statement regarding 'Double Jeopardy' under the BNSS, 2023?
options: Trying a person for two offences committed by him in one incident
Putting the same person on trial twice for the same offence
Trying the same person for two offences at two different times
Trying two persons jointly for the same offence
explanation: Double Jeopardy (embodied in Article 20(2) of the Constitution and Section 337 BNSS) means prosecuting or putting a person on trial twice for the same offence for which he has already been tried and convicted/acquitted.

subject: BNSS
question: The protection against double jeopardy is contained in which Section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 337 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 300 of the old CrPC) provides the statutory bar against double prosecution and trial for the same offence.

subject: BNSS
question: Which one of the following Sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 provides that a person once convicted or acquitted cannot be tried again for the same offence?
explanation: Section 337 is the core provision enforcing the rule of autrefois acquit and autrefois convict under the BNSS, 2023.

subject: BNSS
question: Which Section of the BNSS, 2023 is based on the maxim 'Nemo debet bis vexari pro eadem causa' (no man should be twice vexed for the same cause)?
explanation: The Latin maxim 'Nemo debet bis vexari pro eadem causa' forms the philosophical foundation of Section 337 of the BNSS, 2023.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following Sections is based on the doctrine of 'autrefois acquit' and 'autrefois convict'?
explanation: Autrefois acquit (previously acquitted) and autrefois convict (previously convicted) are common law pleas codified under Section 337 of the BNSS, 2023.

subject: BNSS
question: For the application of Section 337 of the BNSS, 2023, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: There must have been a previous trial of the accused for the same offence
The accused must have been convicted or acquitted in the previous trial for the same offence
The previous proceeding must have been for the same offence
It is not necessary that the court which conducted the trial was competent or not to try the case
explanation: For Section 337 to apply, it is an essential condition that the court which conducted the previous trial must have been a court of competent jurisdiction. Thus, statement D is incorrect.

subject: BNSS
question: A person is charged and convicted by a Magistrate of the second class for the offence of theft. Can he subsequently be charged with and tried for robbery on the same facts?
options: Yes, but only with the permission of the Court of Session
Yes, but only with the permission of the Court by which he was earlier convicted
explanation: Under Section 337(4) of the BNSS, 2023, since a Magistrate of the second class is not competent to try the offence of robbery, the conviction for theft does not bar a subsequent trial for robbery by a competent court. The book answer key lists option A.

subject: BNSS
question: A is tried for voluntarily causing grievous hurt and convicted. The victim subsequently dies as a consequence of the injuries. The State wants to try A for culpable homicide amounting to murder. What is the correct legal position?
options: A cannot be tried for the second time under Section 337 of the BNSS, 2023
A was already convicted and punished and hence cannot be tried second time under the law
A can be tried for the second time for culpable homicide amounting to murder
A can be tried once again for the same offence that caused his death
explanation: Under Section 337(3) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 300(3) CrPC), if a person is convicted of an act causing consequences which constitute a different offence, and those consequences had not happened at the time of conviction, he may be tried again for that offence.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following persons are entitled under Section 339 of the BNSS, 2023 to conduct the prosecution of the case without the permission of the Magistrate?
explanation: Section 339 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 302 of the old CrPC) allows the Public Prosecutor, Assistant PP, or Advocate General to conduct the prosecution without seeking permission from the Magistrate.

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 are provisions for free legal aid to the accused at State expense made?
explanation: Section 341 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 304 of the old CrPC) provides that if the accused has no sufficient means to engage a pleader, the Court of Session (and other courts by notification) shall assign a pleader at State expense.

subject: BNSS
question: Section 341 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 deals with:-
options: Protection of the accused against double prosecution for the same offence
Legal aid to the accused at State expense in certain cases
Order to release on probation of good conduct
explanation: This section codifies the directive principle of equal justice and free legal aid (Article 39A of the Constitution) into the criminal procedure code.

subject: BNSS
question: The court may assign a pleader to an accused in a trial at State expense when it appears to the court that the accused does not have........... means to engage one.
explanation: Under Section 341(1), the statutory standard is 'sufficient means'. If the accused has no 'sufficient means', a pleader must be assigned.

subject: BNSS
question: Where lies the procedure under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 when a corporation or a registered society is an accused?
explanation: Section 342 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 305 of the old CrPC) provides the procedure to be followed when a corporation or registered society is named as an accused.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which provision of law is a body corporate required to appoint an authorized representative for the purpose of an inquiry or trial before a criminal court?
explanation: Section 342(2) provides that a corporation may appoint a representative for the purpose of the inquiry or trial.

subject: BNSS
question: The procedure to be followed when a corporation or registered society is an accused is prescribed in which section of the BNSS, 2023?
explanation: This corresponds to Section 342 of the BNSS, 2023.

subject: BNSS
question: The provision to tender pardon to an accomplice is given in:-
explanation: Section 343 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 306 of the old CrPC) regulates the power to tender pardon to an accomplice at any stage of the inquiry or trial.

subject: BNSS
question: Pardon may be tendered to an accomplice under Section 343 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 when:-
options: he is not in a position to stand trial due to infirm health
he undertakes to make a full and true disclosure of the whole of the circumstances within his knowledge
explanation: Under Section 343(1), the pardon is tendered on the condition that the accomplice makes a full and true disclosure of the facts of the offence.

subject: BNSS
question: To tender a pardon under Section 343 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023:-
options: The witness must not be directly concerned in the offence
The person getting pardon need not be in police custody
Any offence punishable with imprisonment which shall not extend to more than 7 years
explanation: Section 343 applies to offences triable exclusively by the Court of Session or punishable with imprisonment extending to 7 years or more, and there is no requirement that the person getting pardon must be in police custody. The book answer key lists option C.

subject: BNSS
question: Who among the following can tender a pardon to an accomplice under Section 343 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Under Section 343(1), both the CJM (or Metropolitan Magistrate) and a Judicial Magistrate of the first class are empowered to tender a pardon.

subject: BNSS
question: Who among the following is NOT empowered to tender a pardon to an accomplice under Section 343 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Magistrates of the second class do not possess the statutory power to tender a pardon to an accomplice under Section 343.

subject: BNSS
question: When may an accomplice be tendered a pardon under Section 343 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
options: Only at the stage of investigation
Only at the stage of inquiry
Only at the stage of trial
At any stage of enquiry or investigation or the trial
explanation: Under Section 343(1), a pardon may be tendered to an accomplice at any stage of the investigation, inquiry, or trial of the offence.

subject: BNSS
question: A Judicial Magistrate First Class may tender a pardon to a person at any stage of the:-
explanation: Under Section 343(1) of the BNSS, 2023, while the CJM can tender a pardon at any stage including investigation, a Judicial Magistrate of the first class is restricted to tendering it during the inquiry and trial stage only. The book answer key lists option B.

subject: BNSS
question: Who cannot tender a pardon to an accomplice under Section 343 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
options: The Judicial Magistrate First Class while inquiring into or trying the offence
explanation: Pardon power under Section 343 is exclusively judicial; Executive Magistrates have no power to tender a pardon to an accomplice.

subject: BNSS
question: The provisions of Section 343(2) of the BNSS, 2023 regarding tender of pardon to an accomplice apply to offences punishable with imprisonment extending to:-
explanation: Section 343(2) of the BNSS, 2023 specifies that a pardon may be tendered for offences triable exclusively by the Court of Session or punishable with imprisonment which may extend to seven years or with a more severe sentence.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the tender of pardon to an accomplice under Section 343 of the BNSS, 2023?
options: A Chief Judicial Magistrate may tender a pardon at any stage of investigation, inquiry, or trial
A Judicial Magistrate of First Class may tender a pardon at any stage of inquiry or trial
Tender of pardon is not permissible if the offence is punishable with imprisonment of a term exceeding seven years
explanation: Pardon is indeed permissible if the offence is punishable with a term exceeding seven years (in fact, it requires a minimum term of 7 years or a more severe sentence). Hence, statement C is false.

subject: BNSS
question: When an accused person is pardoned under Section 343 of the BNSS, 2023, he:-
options: becomes a witness for the prosecution
should be examined as a witness first in the trial court
becomes a witness for the defence
explanation: Once a pardon is tendered and accepted under Section 343, the accomplice becomes an approver and is examined as a witness for the prosecution.

subject: BNSS
question: Which section of the BNSS, 2023 provides the Court with the power to direct a tender of pardon to the accused before the pronouncement of judgment?
explanation: Section 344 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 307 of the old CrPC) empowers the Court to which the case is committed to tender a pardon at any time before judgment is passed.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 345 of the BNSS, 2023, an accomplice who does not comply with the conditions of pardon may be prosecuted and tried separately for the offence of giving false evidence, but only with the sanction of:-
options: the Chief Justice of High Court
explanation: Section 345(1) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 308(1) CrPC) provides that a trial for the offence of giving false evidence by a pardoned accomplice requires the sanction of the High Court.

subject: BNSS
question: Who is authorized to certify that a person who accepted a tender of pardon under Section 343 or 344 has wilfully concealed material facts or given false evidence, and thus failed to comply with the condition of pardon?
explanation: Under Section 345(1) of the BNSS, 2023, the Public Prosecutor must certify that the person has not complied with the conditions of the pardon, which acts as a prerequisite to prosecution.

subject: BNSS
question: The Principle of Speedy Trial and the statutory limitation period for completing the trial of certain cases are provided under which section of the BNSS, 2023?
explanation: Section 346 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 309 of the old CrPC) provides for day-to-day proceedings, and contains specific timelines for completing investigations and trials.

subject: BNSS
question: When the inquiry or trial relates to a rape offence committed under Section 64 of the BNS, 2023, the inquiry or trial shall be concluded within a period of:-
options: 4 weeks after the filing of charge-sheet
8 weeks after the filing of charge-sheet
2 months after the filing of charge-sheet
4 months after the filing of charge-sheet
explanation: Under Section 346(1) proviso of the BNSS, 2023, the trial for offences under Section 64 (and other sexual offences) shall, as far as possible, be completed within two months from the date of filing of the charge sheet.

subject: BNSS
question: If rape has been committed on a girl under twelve years of age, within which period must the inquiry or trial be completed after the filing of the charge sheet under the BNSS, 2023?
explanation: Like other rape trials under Section 346(1) proviso, trials involving child victims must be completed, as far as possible, within a period of two months from the date of filing of the charge-sheet.

subject: BNSS
question: During an inquiry or trial, under Section 346 of the BNSS, 2023, a Magistrate can remand an accused to custody:-
options: for a maximum of one month at a time
for a maximum of 15 days at a time
for a maximum period of 14 days at a time
for a period till next date irrespective of days
explanation: Under Section 346(2) of the BNSS, 2023, no Magistrate shall remand an accused person to custody under this section for a term exceeding fifteen days at a time.

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following judgments did the Supreme Court determine that if the examination-in-chief of a witness is completed on a particular day, the cross-examination should ideally be completed on the same day?
options: Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab
Ahmad Shah vs. State of Rajasthan
Jasmer Singh vs. State of Haryana
Inder Singh vs. State of Rajasthan
explanation: In Vinod Kumar v. State of Punjab (2015), the Supreme Court strongly condemned the practice of delaying cross-examination after completion of examination-in-chief, mandating that they occur on the same day.

subject: BNSS
question: Can a Magistrate inspect any place of the commission of an offence during a trial under the BNSS, 2023?
options: No, a Magistrate cannot be a witness under Section 347 of the BNSS, 2023
No, a Magistrate is concerned only with the case of the prosecution under Section 347 of the BNSS, 2023
Yes, a Magistrate can inspect any place for the proper appreciation of evidence under Section 347 of the BNSS, 2023
Yes, but the inspection will not be a part of the case file
explanation: Section 347 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 310 of the old CrPC) provides that any Judge or Magistrate may, at any stage of inquiry or trial, visit and inspect any place for the purpose of properly appreciating the evidence.

subject: BNSS
question: Under which section of the BNSS, 2023 does a court at any stage of trial have the power to recall and re-examine any person already examined?
explanation: Section 348 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 311 of the old CrPC) empowers the Court to summon any person as a witness, or examine any person in attendance, or recall and re-examine any person already examined, if their evidence appears essential to the just decision of the case.

subject: BNSS
question: Which provision of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 empowers a criminal court to recall and re-examine witnesses in a criminal case?
explanation: Recall of witnesses can happen under Section 240 (when charges are altered/added) and under Section 348 (discretionary/mandatory power of the court to recall for a just decision).

subject: BNSS
question: The power under Section 348 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 can be exercised by the Court to:-
options: summon any witness who has been cited but not produced or examined before the evidence is closed
summon any witness who has not been cited as a witness
explanation: Section 348 grants wide powers to the court to summon any person as a witness, examine any person present, or recall and re-examine any person already examined, at any stage.

subject: BNSS
question:
Which of the following powers are available to a criminal court under Section 348 of the BNSS, 2023?
i. To summon any person as a witness.
ii. To examine any person in attendance, though not summoned as a witness.
iii. To recall and re-examine any person already examined.
explanation: All three powers (summoning, examining a person present, and recalling/re-examining) are explicitly codified in Section 348.

subject: BNSS
question: What is NOT permissible under Section 348 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
options: Cross-examination of a witness by the court itself
explanation: While the court can examine and recall witnesses to elicit the truth, the court cannot conduct a standard cross-examination of a witness, which is the role of the parties.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following statements is wrong regarding Section 348 of the BNSS, 2023?
options: Under Section 348, witnesses can be recalled at any stage of proceedings
If the evidence of a person appears to be essential to the just decision of the case, the examination under Section 348 is mandatory
The aim of Section 348 is to fill up the gaps in the prosecution's case
All of the above are incorrect
explanation: The primary aim of Section 348 is to discover the truth for a just decision; it cannot be used by the court as a tool to fill up omissions or gaps in the prosecution's case.

subject: BNSS
question: In terms of the provisions of the BNSS, 2023, the power of the Court to recall and re-examine any witness already examined can be exercised:-
options: Before the evidence of the prosecution is closed if the witness is called on the motion of the prosecution
Even after the evidence of both sides is closed
Even after the evidence of the prosecution is closed, but before the evidence of the defence is closed
explanation: The power under Section 348 (old Section 311 CrPC) can be exercised 'at any stage of any inquiry, trial or other proceeding', which includes even after both sides have closed their evidence, prior to the pronouncement of judgment.

subject: BNSS
question: The power conferred under Section 348 of the BNSS, 2023 to summon material witnesses may be utilized by the Court at which stage?
options: any time before closing of prosecution evidence
any time before closing of defence evidence
any time before hearing of final argument
any time before pronouncement of judgment
explanation: The court can summon or recall witnesses under Section 348 at any stage of the trial up until the final judgment is pronounced.

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court hold that the recall of a witness cannot be permitted endlessly on the pretext of a fair trial?
options: State of Haryana v. Ram Mehar (2016)
State of Tamil Nadu v. K. Ramesh (2015)
Pooja Pal v. Union of India (2016)
explanation: In State of Haryana v. Ram Mehar (2016), the Supreme Court emphasized that while fair trial is a right, it does not mean witnesses can be recalled repeatedly to harass them or delay the trial.

subject: BNSS
question: The power of a Magistrate to order any person to provide specimen signatures or handwriting is dealt with under:-
explanation: Section 349 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 311A of the old CrPC) empowers the Magistrate of the first class to order any person to give specimen signatures or handwriting for the purpose of any investigation or proceeding.

subject: BNSS
question: Section 349 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 empowers a Magistrate to:-
options: Proceed against other persons appearing guilty of an offence
Record confession of the accused during trial
Order a person to give specimen signatures or handwriting
Visit and inspect any place in which an offence is alleged to have been committed
explanation: The core power under Section 349 is to direct any person, including an accused, to write specimen signatures or handwriting for comparison.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 349 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which Magistrate is empowered to order a person to give specimen signatures or handwriting?
explanation: Section 349 explicitly empowers a 'Magistrate of the first class' to make such an order.

subject: BNSS
question: Section 349 of the BNSS, 2023 empowers the Magistrate of the First Class to:-
options: Order a person to give specimen signatures
Visit and inspect any place in which an offence is alleged to have been committed
explanation: Section 349 deals exclusively with orders for obtaining specimen signatures or handwriting during investigations or proceedings.

subject: BNSS
question: Under the BNSS, 2023, which provision governs the examination of the accused after the prosecution has closed its evidence?
explanation: Section 351 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 313 of the old CrPC) provides for the examination of the accused to enable him to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidence against him.

subject: BNSS
question: During trial, statements of an accused person are recorded by the court under which section of the BNSS, 2023?
explanation: Recording the statement of the accused to explain incriminating circumstances is done under the power of Section 351.

subject: BNSS
question: The statutory purpose of Section 351 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is:-
options: To know the facts of the case directly from the accused
To enable the accused personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidence against him
To enable the accused to explain his previous bad character
To enable the accused to give evidence of good character
explanation: Section 351(1)(b) mandates the court to question the accused generally on the case after the witnesses for the prosecution have been examined, to allow him to explain any incriminating circumstances.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 351 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the primary purpose of the examination of the accused is to:-
options: enable the accused personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidence against him
enable the accused to know his defence
enable the accused to know about the charges
explanation: The main objective is to establish direct dialogue between the Court and the accused, giving the accused an opportunity to explain the incriminating evidence against him.

subject: BNSS
question: When can the Court put questions to the accused to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidence against him?
options: only after prosecution evidence is over
explanation: Under Section 351(1)(a), the Court may, at any stage of any inquiry or trial, without previously warning the accused, put such questions to him as the Court considers necessary.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 351 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the statement of the accused:-
options: can be either on oath or without oath as per the discretion of the Court
explanation: Section 351(2) of the BNSS, 2023 explicitly states: 'No oath shall be administered to the accused when he is examined under sub-section (1).'

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following options is the administration of an oath NOT required under the BNSS, 2023?
options: Recording of confession under Section 183 of the BNSS, 2023
explanation: No oath is administered to the accused when examined under Section 351, nor is it administered when recording a confession under Section 183.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 351 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023:-
options: No oath shall be administered to the accused when he is examined
The accused shall render himself liable to punishment by refusing to answer questions, or by giving false answers to them
The answers given by the accused cannot be taken into consideration and put in evidence for or against him
Every error or omission in complying with Section 351 necessarily vitiates the trial
explanation: Section 351(2) bars the administration of an oath. The accused is not liable to punishment for refusing to answer or giving false answers (Section 351(3)), and answers can be considered (Section 351(4)).

subject: BNSS
question: Evaluate the statement: "The statement of the accused under Section 351 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is to be recorded on oath."
explanation: The statement is completely false because Section 351(2) explicitly prohibits the administration of an oath to the accused during this examination.

subject: BNSS
question: Which case is related to the power of the Court to examine the accused under Section 313 of the old CrPC (now Section 351 of the BNSS, 2023)?
explanation: The book answer key lists option C, indicating both cases deal with the principles of examining the accused under Section 313 CrPC / Section 351 BNSS.

subject: BNSS
question: In which recent judgment did the Supreme Court summarize the legal proposition regarding the examination of the accused under Section 313 of the Cr.P.C. (now Section 351 of the BNSS, 2023)?
options: C.B.I. Vs. Vikas Mishra @ Vikash Mishra, (2023) 6 SCC 49
Ankit Kothari Vs. State of M.P., ILR 2023 MP 1783
Premchand Vs. State of Maharashtra, (2023) 5 SCC 522
Omprakash Sahni Vs. Jai Shankar Choudhary & Anr., (2023) 5 SCC 123
explanation: In Premchand v. State of Maharashtra (2023), the Supreme Court summarized the guidelines, noting that the examination is not a mere formality and the court must put all incriminating circumstances to the accused.

subject: BNSS
question: Which section of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 provides that the person accused of an offence shall be a competent defence witness?
explanation: Section 353 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 315 of the old CrPC) provides that an accused person is a competent witness for the defence and may give evidence on oath in disproof of the charges.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the accused testifying as a defence witness under the BNSS, 2023?
options: Accused person shall not be called as a witness by any party
Accused person shall not be called as a witness except on his own request in writing
Accused may give evidence on oath in disproof of the charges made against him
Failure of the accused to give evidence shall not give rise to any presumption against himself
explanation: Stating that the 'accused shall not be called as a witness by any party' without qualification is incomplete. Under Section 353, he *can* be called, but strictly *only* upon his own request in writing. The book answer key lists option A.

subject: BNSS
question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, can an accused person be a competent witness in his own defence?
options: On his own request in writing
With the leave of Court of Session
With the leave of CJM only
explanation: Section 353(1) proviso (a) mandates that the accused shall not be called as a witness except on his own request in writing.

subject: BNSS
question: In a criminal trial, an accused person:-
options: May be examined as a witness in his defence but only on his own request in writing
May be examined as a witness in his defence but only on his own request made orally
May be examined as a witness in his defence and if he does not do so an adverse inference may be drawn against him
May be examined as a witness in his defence if the court so directs
explanation: An accused can choose to testify as a defence witness, but it must be initiated by his written request, and his failure to do so cannot be commented upon or raise any adverse presumption.

subject: BNSS
question: A Court may commence the trial against an absconded proclaimed offender under Section 356 of the BNSS, 2023 after the lapse of a period of:-
explanation: Section 356 of the BNSS, 2023 is a newly added provision that allows the trial of a proclaimed offender in absentia after the lapse of ninety days from the date of framing of the charge.

subject: BNSS
question: What is the period of limitation to file an appeal against conviction by a proclaimed offender tried in absentia under Section 356 of the BNSS, 2023?
explanation: Under Section 356(8) of the BNSS, 2023, a proclaimed offender convicted in absentia has a limitation period of three years to appeal against the conviction, subject to showing sufficient cause.

subject: BNSS
question: If the accused, though not of unsound mind, cannot be made to understand the proceedings, the Court:-
options: may proceed with the inquiry or trial
will forward the proceeding to the High Court
explanation: Section 357 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 318 of the old CrPC) provides that if the accused cannot understand the proceedings, the court may proceed with the inquiry or trial.

subject: BNSS
question: If the accused, though not of unsound mind, cannot be made to understand the proceedings of the court, the court (other than High Court) may proceed with the inquiry or trial, but if such proceedings result in conviction:-
options: the court shall pronounce the judgement according to law
the court shall postpone the proceedings till the accused recovers and becomes able to understand the proceedings
the court shall forward the proceedings to the Sessions Judge with a report of the circumstances
the court shall forward the proceedings with a report of the circumstances of the case to the High Court
explanation: Under Section 357, if a court (other than High Court) convicts an accused who could not understand the proceedings, the court must stay the signing of the sentence and forward the proceedings to the High Court, which will pass appropriate orders.

subject: BNSS
question: In the case of an accused facing inquiry or trial who is not of unsound mind but is incapable of understanding the proceedings:-
options: the court shall proceed with the inquiry or trial
the court shall not proceed with the inquiry or trial
the court may proceed with the inquiry or trial after obtaining necessary orders from the High Court

the court may proceed with the inquiry or trial, and if the case results in conviction, forward the proceeding to the High Court along with a report on which the High Court shall pass such orders as deemed fit
explanation: This details the full statutory mechanism of Section 357 BNSS (old Section 318 CrPC) where a conviction triggers a reference to the High Court.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 358 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (power to proceed against other persons appearing to be guilty), a person may be added as an additional accused on the basis of:-
options: documents relied on by the prosecution
supplementary report of the investigating officer
explanation: Section 358 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 319 of the old CrPC) provides that the court can proceed against any person not being an accused if it appears 'from the evidence' that such person has committed an offence.

subject: BNSS
question: If evidence is available during a trial about a person who appears to have committed an offence but is not mentioned in the charge-sheet as an accused:-
options: his name can be added by the Judicial Magistrate/Sessions Court
his name cannot be added at this stage
his name can be added by the High Court only
his name can be added by the Supreme Court only
explanation: Section 358 empowers the trial court (Magistrate or Sessions Court) to summon and try such a person along with the other accused.

subject: BNSS
question: While exercising power under Section 358 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the Court can:-
options: Not summon a person who is not named in FIR
Not summon a person who is named in the FIR but not charge-sheeted
Summon a person who has been discharged without complying with Sections 337 and 439 of the BNSS, 2023
explanation: The power under Section 358 is very broad and is not restricted by whether the person was named in the FIR or left out of the charge-sheet. The book answer key lists option D.

subject: BNSS
question: The landmark judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 3 SCC 92, deals with:-
options: Section 311 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 [Now, Section 348 of B.N.S.S.]
Section 41 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 [Now, Section 35 of B.N.S.S.]
Section 313 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 [Now, Section 351 of B.N.S.S.]
Section 319 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 [Now, Section 358 of B.N.S.S.]
explanation: In Hardeep Singh v. State of Punjab (2014), a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court settled the law regarding the scope, stage, and standard of evidence required to invoke Section 319 CrPC (now Section 358 BNSS).

subject: BNSS
question: The Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 'Hardeep Singh vs State of Punjab' (2014) 3 SCC 92 clarified the ambit and scope of:-
explanation: The Hardeep Singh judgment is the definitive authority explaining the powers of the criminal court to array additional accused during a trial.

subject: BNSS
question: In which of the following cases did a Five-Judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court consider the scope and ambit of Section 319 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 (now Section 358 of the BNSS, 2023)?
options: Hardeep Singh v. State of Punjab
S. Mohammed Ispahani v. Yogendra Chandak
explanation: Hardeep Singh v. State of Punjab (2014) is the landmark Constitution Bench ruling that exhaustively laid down rules on the power of the Court to summon additional accused.

subject: BNSS
question: The landmark case of Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab and Others (2014) is primarily concerned with the issue of:-
options: Power of Court to proceed against other persons appearing to be guilty of offence
Procedure in case of accused being lunatic
explanation: This case dealt with the scope of Section 319 of the old CrPC (now Section 358 of the BNSS, 2023) regarding adding non-accused persons to a trial.

subject: BNSS
question: Which landmark Constitution Bench ruling of the Supreme Court resolved conflicting decisions regarding a criminal Court's power to add additional accused in a trial?
options: Hardeep Singh vs. State of Punjab & others
Ranjit Singh vs. State of Punjab
Hema Mishra vs. State of U.P.
explanation: The Constitution Bench in Hardeep Singh (2014) resolved the conflict between previous rulings like Ranjit Singh and Dharam Pal regarding the stage at which Section 319 CrPC (now Section 358 BNSS) can be invoked.

subject: BNSS
question: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that a person can be summoned as an additional accused under Section 319 CrPC (now Section 358 BNSS) even on the basis of the examination-in-chief of a witness, and that the Court need not wait for their cross-examination?
options: Sartaj Singh v. State of Haryana & Another
Budhdev Karmaskar v. State of West Bengal
Jacob Puliyal v. Union of India
State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai
explanation: In Sartaj Singh v. State of Haryana (2021), the Supreme Court reiterated that examination-in-chief constitutes 'evidence' under Section 319 CrPC (now Section 358 BNSS) and the court can summon a person without waiting for cross-examination.

subject: BNSS
question: Offences in which a compromise can be arrived at between the parties under Section 359 of the BNSS, 2023 are termed:-
explanation: Section 359 of the BNSS, 2023 (corresponding to Section 320 of the old CrPC) deals with compoundable offences, which allow a compromise between the victim and the accused.

subject: BNSS
question: The statutory classification of compoundable and non-compoundable offences has been provided under which section of the BNSS, 2023?
explanation: Section 359 of the BNSS, 2023 contains tables listing compoundable offences (sub-section (1) without court permission, and sub-section (2) with court permission).

subject: BNSS
question: An offence can be compounded under Section 359 of the BNSS, 2023 at which stage of the proceedings?
explanation: Under Section 359(5) and (6) of the BNSS, 2023, compounding is allowed during trial, appeal (with permission of the appellate court), or revision (with permission of the High Court/Sessions Court). The book answer key lists option D.

subject: BNSS
question: Who is the competent person to compound the offence of 'Theft' under Section 359 of the BNSS, 2023?
options: the station house officer where F.I.R. of stolen property is lodged
explanation: As per the table in Section 359, the compounding of theft can be done by 'the owner of the property stolen' with the permission of the Court.

subject: BNSS
question: When a person who would otherwise be competent to compound an offence under Section 359 of the BNSS, 2023 is under the age of eighteen years, then:-
options: Legal representative of such person may compound the offence without permission of the court
Legal representative of such person may compound the offence with the permission of the court
Any person competent to contract on his behalf, may, with the permission of the court, compound such an offence
explanation: Section 359(4)(a) of the BNSS, 2023 provides that when a person is under eighteen years or is an idiot/lunatic, any person competent to contract on his behalf may, with the permission of the Court, compound such offence.

subject: BNSS
question: When a person competent to compound an offence under Section 359 of the BNSS, 2023 is an idiot or a lunatic, who can compound the offence on their behalf?
options: The legal representative of such person may compound the offence without permission of the Court
The legal representative of such person may compound the offence with the permission of the Court
Any person competent to contract on his behalf, with the permission of the Court
explanation: Under Section 359(4)(a), for a lunatic or idiot, a contract-competent person (like a guardian) can compound with the Court's permission.

subject: BNSS
question: If the person who is competent to compound an offence under Section 359 of the BNSS, 2023 is dead, how can the compounding be effected?
options: Can be done by the legal representative of the deceased without the permission of the court
Can be done by the legal representative of the deceased with the permission of the court
explanation: Section 359(4)(b) of the BNSS, 2023 provides that when the person competent to compound is dead, the legal representative (as defined in the CPC) of such person may, with the consent of the Court, compound such offence.

subject: BNSS
question: Under Section 359 of the BNSS, 2023, if the person who would otherwise be competent to compound is deceased, then:-
options: a legal representative of such person as defined in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, can compound the offence with the consent of the Court
the offence can be compounded by any eyewitness
the offence cannot be compounded after the death of the person
a legal representative of such person as defined in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, can compound the offence with the consent of the Court
explanation: The legal representative (under Section 2(11) of the CPC) can compound the offence, but only with the consent/permission of the Court (Options A and D are identical in the book, and key lists D).

subject: BNSS
question: In a criminal case instituted on the complaint of the Public Prosecutor regarding defamation of a Minister in respect of his public functions, how can the offence be compounded?
options: the offence is compoundable by the Public Prosecutor without the permission of the Court
the offence is compoundable by the Public Prosecutor with the permission of the Court
the offence is compoundable by the person defamed with the permission of the Court
explanation: Under Section 359, defamation (including that of a Minister under Section 222 BNSS) is compoundable by 'the person defamed' with the permission of the Court.

subject: BNSS
question: 'A' is convicted of a cognizable offence of Cheating involving Rs. 50 lakhs. During the pendency of the appeal, what power does the Appellate Court have regarding compounding?
options: Can compound the offence having the effect of conviction
Can compound the offence having the effect of acquittal
Has no option to compound but to hear the appeal on merits
explanation: Section 359(5) allows the appellate court to permit the compounding of a compoundable offence, and Section 359(8) states that compounding shall have the effect of an acquittal.

subject: BNSS
question: The compounding of an offence under Section 359 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 shall have the statutory effect of:-
explanation: Section 359(8) of the BNSS, 2023 (old Section 320(8) CrPC) explicitly provides that the compounding of an offence under this section shall have the effect of an acquittal of the accused.

subject: BNSS
question: Which of the following statements in respect of Section 359 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, is incorrect?
options: The compounding of an offence before charge shall have the effect of discharge of the accused
No offence shall be compounded if the accused is, by reason of a previous conviction, liable to enhanced punishment
When an appeal is pending, composition for the offence shall be allowed without the leave of the appellate court
The person competent to compound an offence is dead, the legal representative of such person may, with the consent of the court, compound such offence
explanation: Compounding at any stage (pre-charge or post-charge) always has the effect of an acquittal, not a discharge. Thus, statement A is incorrect.

subject: BNSS
question: Offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) other than those specifically mentioned in Section 359 of the BNSS, 2023 are:-
options: compoundable with the permission of court
compoundable by the Court of Sessions
